notes.title: Update 0.9.5
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/9e74b8471f37bfe4a357bff8235e232b902d6626.jpg[/img]

[h1]Gameplay changes:[/h1][olist]
[*][h1][b]3 missions for the Allies have been added: [/b][/h1]
Operation Lightfoot, [b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/282995674665717888]The Invasion of Normandy / D-Day[/url][/b], and The Battle of Anzio!

[*] [h1][b]New commanders have been introduced![/b][/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/262300d789250a9151fc32e15789ba77fc5ae4a6.jpg[/img]

[h1]For the Axis: Commander of Artillery [b]Georg von Küchler[/b]![/h1]

Georg von Küchler was one of the authors of the German doctrine of combined arms reconnaissance. He participated in World War I, where he received many orders and medals for his actions. In 1919, he volunteered to go to Poland to fight the Red Army. During World War II, he took part in the invasions of Poland, the Netherlands, and Belgium. In 1944, he was forced to resign, but when he was offered a chance to join the plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler known as the 20 July Plot, he refused it. Coming from a family of German officers, he was a real patriot of his Fatherland and believed in its ideals. Küchler learned all of the advantages of conducting reconnaissance in force when he was in Poland. For this purpose, he uses snipers, light vehicles, and anti-tank artillery supported by infantry and assault infantry. His views on defensive warfare were formed under the influence of constant redeployments from one front to another. That's why he prefers light and mobile squads with anti-tank rifles, mortars, and anti-tank guns rather than permanent fortifications.

[i]Premium Units for reaching new levels:[/i]
1) SdKfz 231 + Pz IVe;
2) 2 Wespe;
3) SdKfz 234 Puma + Sturmtiger!

[h1]For the Allies: Infantry Commander [b]Claude Auchinleck[/b]![/h1]

Claude Auchinleck was a British military commander, knight (by June 1945), and Field Marshal. During World War I he took part in military operations in Egypt, Aden, and Mesopotamia. He was one of the most respected commanders in the British Army. In 1941 he was appointer Commander-in-Chief in India, then he was sent to North Africa to replace Field Marshal A. Wavell as Commander-in-Chief, British Middle East Command. He started preparing an advance operation against German and Italian troops under the command of General Rommel (Operation Crusader). Despite heavy casualties, Auchinleck managed to have some success (breaking the siege of Tobruk). After that, however, Rommel counter-attacked, captured Benghazi on 29th January 1942, and pushed the British forces back to Gazala and Bir Hakeim. Auchinleck moved his reserves up and launched a new attack, defeating Rommel in July 1942 in the Battle of El Alamein.

[i]Premium Units for reaching new levels:[/i]
1) Assault Infantry + Panhard 178;
2) 2 rare Anti-Tank Infantry squads;
3) Machine Gunners and Greyhound!

[*] [h1][b]We have re-worked and improved the characteristics of the units:[/b][/h1]
- Characteristics have become more authentic;
- Now units of different eras are closer in strength; 
Previously units of an older era used to be much stronger than those of the previous one. We have balanced these limits, and now it's the unit's historical characteristics that affect its strength, not a link to a particular period of the war; 
- We have corrected armor characteristics: thanks to your help we found some inconsistencies in our characteristics and corrected them!
- Additional balance improvements. 

[*] [h1] [b]Assault mode has undergone significant changes![/b][/h1]
- We have increased the maximum number of initial troops and the reinforcement limit for the attacker and the defender;
- We have changed Reinforcement Point generation and bonuses for capturing Control Points.[/olist]

[i]P.S. Visit our [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/282995674661774824][b]Development Blog[/b][/url] to read a new post about the history of Assault mode! :)[/i]

[i]Premium Units for reaching new levels:[/i]
1) SdKfz 231 + Pz IVe;
2) 2 Wespe;
3) SdKfz 234 Puma + Sturmtiger!

[h1]For the Allies: Infantry Commander [b]Claude Auchinleck[/b]![/h1]

Claude Auchinleck was a British military commander, knight (by June 1945), and Field Marshal. During World War I he took part in military operations in Egypt, Aden, and Mesopotamia. He was one of the most respected commanders in the British Army. In 1941 he was appointer Commander-in-Chief in India, then he was sent to North Africa to replace Field Marshal A. Wavell as Commander-in-Chief, British Middle East Command. He started preparing an advance operation against German and Italian troops under the command of General Rommel (Operation Crusader). Despite heavy casualties, Auchinleck managed to have some success (breaking the siege of Tobruk). After that, however, Rommel counter-attacked, captured Benghazi on 29th January 1942, and pushed the British forces back to Gazala and Bir Hakeim. Auchinleck moved his reserves up and launched a new attack, defeating Rommel in July 1942 in the Battle of El Alamein.

[i]Premium Units for reaching new levels:[/i]
1) Assault Infantry + Panhard 178;
2) 2 rare Anti-Tank Infantry squads;
3) Machine Gunners and Greyhound!

[*] [h1][b]We have re-worked and improved the characteristics of the units:[/b][/h1]
- Characteristics have become more authentic;
- Now units of different eras are closer in strength; 
Previously units of an older era used to be much stronger than those of the previous one. We have balanced these limits, and now it's the unit's historical characteristics that affect its strength, not a link to a particular period of the war; 
- We have corrected armor characteristics: thanks to your help we found some inconsistencies in our characteristics and corrected them!
- Additional balance improvements. 

[*] [h1] [b]Assault mode has undergone significant changes![/b][/h1]
- We have increased the maximum number of initial troops and the reinforcement limit for the attacker and the defender;
- We have changed Reinforcement Point generation and bonuses for capturing Control Points.[/olist]

[i]P.S. Visit our [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/282995674661774824][b]Development Blog[/b][/url] to read a new post about the history of Assault mode! :)[/i]

notes.title: D-day mission!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/f7ad97c119fd84ce0b993fd82f0e2f257fd1ceb1.jpg[/img]

[h1]Dear officers, we welcome you to join the most powerful landing operation in history, often known as [b]D-Day, the Invasion of Normandy![/b] [/h1]

On the 6th of June, 1944, Allied troops begin landing operations in the north of France. This operation will become one if the most important events in WW II history. The intrusion included two stages of monumental scope. 
The first stage was an airborne operation during which 24,000 British, American, Canadian, and French paratroopers landed on the shore in Normandy. 

The second stage was an amphibious operation that became the largest operation in world history with the simultaneous sea entry of 156,000 solders, with 195,700 seamen supporting and the cojoined participation of almost 7000 battle and transport ships of all types.

The landing of Allied forces, marking the opening of the second fighting line in West Europe, became an important factor in the fight against the Axis powers. Germany was caught in a vice from both the west and east, and forced to fight on two fronts. The new theatre of war blocked German forces that could have been relocated as a last-ditch hope to fight off the advancing Russian army. Thus, ultimate victory was achieved sooner and with fewer casualties. The western frontline became a true symbol of the union of the Allied Forces. 

[h1]There is no way we could overlook this landmark event in our game. So we have put forth tremendous effort to create an exciting mission![/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/0382dac38af52a828536cca8aeafa69e4401960a.jpg[/img]

Your goal in the D-Day mission is to support the sea landing and crush the enemy forces on the approaches to Caen.

[h1]A playthrough will include two stages: [/h1]

Firstly, you will control a few special forces groups that landed on Utah Beach. The main goal will be to destroy artillery weapons spotted from the air in a rear attack. Without your help, your allies on Omaha Beach will suffer significant losses! Shot down with precision by the Germans, reinforcements have been prevented from reaching several beach fronts where they are sorely needed! Halt the seemingly never-ending fire of the German artillery to save hundreds of lives!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/5e89a3655dd3a595bf1debcfa9ea65a6c4274874.jpg[/img]

[h1]The mentioned storyline resonates with the true historic events. [/h1]
On the 6th of June, 1944, Richard Winters led an attack on a German 105mm howitzer battery. With only 13 men against roughly fifty germans in fortified positions, Richard took down artillery squads one by one. This operation went down in history as "The Battle at Brécourt Manor" and to this day serves as an excellent example of a skilled small tactical squad attack against stationary enemy positions. 

But that wasn’t the end of the path for Winters. His party progressed even further, directly to Brécourt Manor. Richard’s orders to his men were clear and simple:  «Fire on the bushes there, there, and there, and the house itself. Just level to the ground anything that sticks up above it.» 

You are about to repeat Winters’s heroic act: destroy all enemy objects of strategic importance with a handful of units. Choose effective actions to minimise casualties and show yourself as a true hero!
You will unlock new opportunities as you progress in fortifying positions and neutralise dangerous weapons: you and your allies will be able to call in reinforcements and aviation. Together you can seize this vitally important victory!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/50382ea6dd8029f2c6a2946c5d521802807683ff.jpg[/img]

[b]The second stage of the operation [/b]will be supporting the assault of the Allied Forces and fortifying positions near the outskirts of Caen. While you were fighting from Utah Beach side, the Allied Forces on Omaha Beach have not been wasting time: “...it was a challenge for the tanks... but they saved the day by launching heavy fire on the Germans and receiving heavy fire in kind”. But without your support they are doomed to die!

As you progress through the far Caen outskirts towards Omaha beach, neutralising carefully fortified German weapons, you find out that a deadly threat is moving toward the Allied Forces - a tank division. Defeat will be imminent if the division makes it to the troops on the beach with a full complement! Your fellow soldiers will die, and any hope to call in reinforcements will be lost! 

You have to crush the immense enemy forces, including the units hidden in the city streets, before the Allied Forces can dig in in the Caen suburbs. Tigers and Panthers will be waiting for you in the narrow streets, and only the competent involvement of the officership, represented by you, will allows us to reverse the tide of battle and drive the enemy out of strategic areas. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/5dcd0a261d966d90d7ab90e92c6184117e00d90e.jpg[/img]

[h1]Make haste to victory in one of the most recognisable, important, and bloody battles of WW II! [/h1]

notes.title: Development Blog #30
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/66bcba8d345b105794050adb7a6b8c5247baaea8.jpg[/img]

[h1]Greetings, commanders![/h1]

Today in our development blog we are going to tell you about an important change that will affect Blitzkrieg 3 gameplay soon. Many of you were worried about Assault mode, which has gradually become less exciting than it used to be. We have good news for you: changes are coming soon! But first, let's dive into the project's past and remember where this whole thing started.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/23990a28de55916df3597a2b50053a1edcf8116e.jpg[/img]

[h1]Initially, Blitzkrieg 3 was a game oriented towards asynchronous gameplay. [/h1]We didn't intend to have two players on the battlefield at the same time, and the essence of the Assault was making your uneasy way towards your enemy's base. 

[h1]But many of you were interested in fighting against other players, so we decided to add a synchronous component to the game, too. [/h1]That wasn't easy to add – we had to significantly rework our existing content. 

We threw all our efforts at creating a new dynamic battle system that would work in Skirmish, the classic RTS mode. We also had a number of other things to do: we added a loyalty system for generals, re-worked the PvE component, and presented the new Axis campaign to you. All in all, we have almost completely remade our game. 

[h1]As a result, Assault mode was temporarily ignored. You have reminded us of this many times, so we have decided to get down to updating it significantly.[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/3033a795ce09491b2826737bb22078020c0f2fbb.png[/img]

You can currently only assign a small number of troops to attack or defend, so the number of effective tactics available is limited. Some players started to feel that Assault mode was too linear and primitive. We want it to be more complex and strategically sophisticated as you exercise your commanding skill, both on the offensive as well as the defensive. 

[h1]So with your help, we are planning to update Assault mode, making it more interesting and attractive for the Blitzkrieg 3 community. [/h1]Here's a list of the things we are planning to do:[olist]
[*]We will increase the attacker's and defender's unit limits and reduce the rate of reserve point generation (whether a human player or an AI is opposing the player). This will let you devise more interesting, diverse defensive tactics, and it'll be harder to capture enemy HQ. The importance of creating a strong army will still be there, and a successful Assault will require even more units than it used to.

[*]These changes will affect balance, too. The Bomber, for instance, has become more powerful and more dangerous. We decided to make it more powerful after considering your feedback in threads related to unit characteristics. We have already announced that we are changing the characteristics, with reference to data from Blitzkrieg 1. You may be surprised at this, but around 80% of the characteristics in parts 1 and 3 of the franchise are the same! But this doesn't mean that the next update's characteristics will be final. We are trying to make our game as historically accurate as possible, and if you notice any inaccuracy, feel free to contact us. We will verify your information and make the characteristics even more accurate and authentic.

[*]We are planning to make the defender also capable of digging trenches. 

[*]You asked us to add an option to watch replays of base attacks. In response, we are restoring this function to the game. This option will help you analyse your defense and improve and develop it so that not a single enemy can reach your HQ!

[*]We would like to remind you that you can get decent rewards for victory in an asynchronous Assault right now, as you can in a Skirmish battle. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/bfbb5183ba1d3bc4261a47b71faa34806658a0d9.jpg[/img]

[i]P.S. One more thing worth adding: thanks to your reports, we have found and fixed an annoying bug. This bug made the AI call in reinforcements made up of units from earlier eras. For example, if you assaulted a 3rd era base, the defender would call in 1st era tanks. This won't happen anymore.[/i]

[h1]Comrades, don't forget about [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/282995674658078644]the Game Barks Contest[/url] going on now![/h1]Participating is easy: all it takes is a little imagination! Don't miss your chance to win valuable prizes and contribute to the game's development!

notes.title: Game Barks Contest!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/7649cee7c146cc7b754a656d646239791fc47bf6.jpg[/img]

Greetings, officers!

[b][h1]We hereby announce the start of the Game Barks Contest![/h1][/b]

What are "barks"? They're the lines you hear your units say throughout the game. The following popular phrases are examples of barks from the first games of the Blitzkrieg series:

1) They won't know what hit 'em!
2) Where is the bad guys?
3) Sweetheart, you've heard the man!
4) Right'a, w-we're rollin'...

[b]We would like you to contribute to the project: units will speak the phrases you submit![/b]

They can be cues for units of any nation, used in specific game situations – or phrases to be uttered by the characters throughout the game. 

[h1]We have a list of categories you can use when writing your cues:  [/h1]
[olist]
[*][h1]Tutorial[/h1]
Commentary during the Tutorial. 
Examples: "Press the Attack button", "Capture the watchtower".

[*][h1]Completing missions and achieving results[/h1]
Phrases uttered when completing missions and achieving results.
Examples: "Watchtower captured!", "AA guns destroyed!", "Kryukov is saved!"

[*][h1]Requesting Support[/h1]
Calling in recon aircraft, attack aircraft, a bomber, a fighter, or paratroopers. A request for a howitzer salvo or smoke screen (by an ally or by an enemy).
Examples: "Aviation will cover you", "Fighter requested by the enemy".

[*][h1]Spotting an enemy[/h1]
A unit or support (reconnaissance aircraft) spots an enemy.
Examples: "Enemy spotted", "There's a Kraut behind that AA gun!"

[*][h1]Reaction to combat actions[/h1]
Possible situations: your squad is running low on health, an enemy is killed, a ricochet, missing the target, a massive attack, infantry approaching a tank and receiving a buff.
Examples: "Too tough to pierce!", "Burn, bastard!", "Good to have an APC nearby..."

[*][h1]Reaction to debuffing [/h1]
What we mean here is when a negative effect is applied to units. Optics are damaged, a track is blown off.
For example: "A round is stuck in the chamber!"

[*][h1]Reaction to the terrain [/h1]
The troops comment on the nearby terrain and its advantages and disadvantages.
For example: "Good place for an ambush", "Another bog to cross..."

[*][h1]Reaction to staying idle[/h1]
Example: "Hey Kryukov, are you asleep again?", "So, are we gonna open fire or what?"[/olist]

[i]If you have an interesting phrase that does not fall under these categories, you are welcome to submit it, too! :)[/i]

[b][h1]Contest terms:[/h1][/b][olist]
[*]Develop and post a set of bark phrases for units in the special thread created for this purpose [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/0/154643214752869155/]ON STEAM[/url] and [url=http://en.blitzkrieg.com/forum/showthread.php?t=2346&p=5648#post5648]FORUM[/url] by 23:59 Moscow time, December 21. 
[*]Each phrase should have a comment: who says it and in what particular situation or mission.
[*]You can come up with any number of phrases, but quality is better than quantity.
[*]Your work must comply with Russian law, the User Agreement, and the rules of the forum.
[*]Plagiarism, i.e. passing off someone else's work as your own, is forbidden.[/olist]

[b][h1]Announcement of the results and awards:[/h1][/b][list]
[*]The most interesting phrases will be added to the game, and their authors will get great prizes!
[*]Three winners will get a legendary tank of their choice.
[*]These players' names will also appear in the project credits.
[*]Authors of phrases we like which don't make it to the top three will be able to choose one of the following tanks: Pz.Kpfw. VI Tiger, SdFkz 234 Puma, SdKfz 165 Hummel, SdKfz 186 Jagdtiger, Pz.Kpfw. VI Tiger II, KV-2, KV-85, T-44, IS-2, ISU-152, T26E1 Super Pershing, Sherman Caliope, Churchill, M4A3E8.
[*]The results will be announced on 13th of January.
[/list]

[b][h1]Important![/h1][/b][list]
[*]It is no secret that there will be an account wipe before the game is released. Don't worry about your prizes: we will re-award them to the winners after the wipe!
[*]The administration fully reserves the right to use the participants' bark phrases for its own purposes.[/list]

[h1]Let's work together to make our game even more interesting![/h1]
 
The administration reserves the right to change this event's procedure at any time, provided that the players are informed via the publishing of such changes on the website or the game forum. The administration is entitled to make final decisions on any controversial issues.

Example: "Hey Kryukov, are you asleep again?", "So, are we gonna open fire or what?"[/olist]

[i]If you have an interesting phrase that does not fall under these categories, you are welcome to submit it, too! :)[/i]

[b][h1]Contest terms:[/h1][/b][olist]
[*]Develop and post a set of bark phrases for units in the special thread created for this purpose [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/0/154643214752869155/]ON STEAM[/url] and [url=http://en.blitzkrieg.com/forum/showthread.php?t=2346&p=5648#post5648]FORUM[/url] by 23:59 Moscow time, December 21. 
[*]Each phrase should have a comment: who says it and in what particular situation or mission.
[*]You can come up with any number of phrases, but quality is better than quantity.
[*]Your work must comply with Russian law, the User Agreement, and the rules of the forum.
[*]Plagiarism, i.e. passing off someone else's work as your own, is forbidden.[/olist]

[b][h1]Announcement of the results and awards:[/h1][/b][list]
[*]The most interesting phrases will be added to the game, and their authors will get great prizes!
[*]Three winners will get a legendary tank of their choice.
[*]These players' names will also appear in the project credits.
[*]Authors of phrases we like which don't make it to the top three will be able to choose one of the following tanks: Pz.Kpfw. VI Tiger, SdFkz 234 Puma, SdKfz 165 Hummel, SdKfz 186 Jagdtiger, Pz.Kpfw. VI Tiger II, KV-2, KV-85, T-44, IS-2, ISU-152, T26E1 Super Pershing, Sherman Caliope, Churchill, M4A3E8.
[*]The results will be announced on 13th of January.
[/list]

[b][h1]Important![/h1][/b][list]
[*]It is no secret that there will be an account wipe before the game is released. Don't worry about your prizes: we will re-award them to the winners after the wipe!
[*]The administration fully reserves the right to use the participants' bark phrases for its own purposes.[/list]

[h1]Let's work together to make our game even more interesting![/h1]
 
The administration reserves the right to change this event's procedure at any time, provided that the players are informed via the publishing of such changes on the website or the game forum. The administration is entitled to make final decisions on any controversial issues.

notes.title: First Allies campaign missions are available!
notes.content:
[img]http://s018.radikal.ru/i514/1612/da/b69b98887631.jpg[/img]

Greetings, officers!
[h1][b]Hurry up to be the first ones to try out the first Allies’ missions![/b][/h1]
Repeat Wavell’s heroic deed and capture the Italian headquarters in Libya!
Save comrades from the occupied territories of Crete!
Help free the besieged Tobruk!
Bring long-awaited victories to the Allies!

We present you a brief historical background on each one of the three missions!

[h1]1. The Libyan Operation [/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/8ae12c9fec4cc59a74c0de1e6ef970489ceecadc.jpg[/img]

In September 1940, Italian forces under the command of Rodolfo Graziani invaded British-controlled Egypt. However, after advancing only a few dozen kilometres into the country, the Italians stopped their offensive and set up camp.
Despite being clearly outnumbered—36,000 Allied troops against 150,000 on the Italian side—the British commander Archibald Wavell decided to strike with full force at the enemy forces. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/bfa539b7b9a5accd89e4e4853fa2cca1622481dc.jpg[/img]

Your objective is to capture the Italian HQ, thereby changing the course of the war.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/5476382365d701961919283ea6682dbf0154b09f.jpg[/img]

[h1]2. The Battle of Crete. Operation Mercury[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/67f9eae253ae826c1075c069c7d14b362bb2cf23.jpg[/img]

In order to establish complete strategic control over the Mediterranean Basin and definitively drive Allied forces out from it, the German command decided to occupy Crete. 
However, it proved unassailable: the British navy was in full control of the coastal waters, while a garrison of 42,000 Allied troops had been stationed on the island itself. To break through the defences, the Germans decided to conduct a large-scale airborne operation. 
Despite heavy losses, Hitler’s army succeeded in its plan. Chances to save the civilians, as well as some of the troops, are extremely small. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/be51f2e0285532e3de2e703fd1f490361e0feb7f.jpg[/img]

You will be tasked with evacuating staff officers and AA gunners from an airport that has been captured by the Germans. Remember that a fierce battle is being fought all around you, so you must act with extreme caution! Your intervention is the only chance to preserve the lives of at least some of the troops on the island.

[h1]3. The Relief of Tobruk. Operation Crusader[/h1]

In March 1941, German troops under the command of Erwin Rommel routed the British and drove them out of Libya. The British garrison in Tobruk found itself under siege.

The first attempt at relieving the siege was unsuccessful. After meticulous preparations, British forces conducted another offensive on the 18th of November, but failed to achieve victory again. On the 21st of November, Rommel counterattacked and tried to seize the initiative. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/fee9c67eda8c00d7efd21f7a17ad4883d8a92f3d.jpg[/img]

You will be tasked with conducting a difficult but important operation. In order to break the string of defeats, German forces must be cut off from their reserves—or the Allied armies will be reduced to mere handfuls of soldiers. The Germans are persistently attacking the 4th Indian Division, and chances of victory are diminishing by the day. If you manage to deny fuel to the enemy, the Allied forces will be able to continue their attack and liberate the besieged Tobruk.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/d1e5aac2150883ab89de4075b8a7a2a939b1d5a8.jpg[/img]

[i]Hurry up to be the first ones to claim victory on the new territories!
See you on the battlefield![/i]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/52ea3c94c81750ace0505ee09c14214d7b5470ec.jpg[/img]

notes.content:

[h1]Gameplay changes:[/h1][olist]
[*] Added [b]Quick Save[/b] feature!
Below is the explanation of how the Quick Save feature will work.
You have only one savegame slot available at a time.
You can load the game:
During a mission;
If you fail a mission you made the save in;
If you quit the game or connection to server was lost.

[*]In Rebellion in Warsaw mission you can save the Home Army even after you saved Armia Ludowa now.

notes.title: Development Blog #29
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/29/flow.jpg[/img]

Greetings, dear commanders!
Today we’ve got a run-down of the in-game camera controls, details on upcoming changes to commanders, some new statistics to share, and of course; we’d like to know what new commanders you’d like to see added to the game.

[h1]1. Camera[/h1]

The game already allows you to control the camera with the Insert and Home keys. However, if you try moving the camera this way, it won't return to the standard position. 
For your convenience we plan to transfer the controls from these keys to the mouse wheel. By pressing and holding it, you'll be able to rotate the camera, with another click returning it to its initial position.

[h1]2. Commanders[/h1]

We have re-worked all of the commanders, making each of them truly unique. Their bonuses cover 8 types of units: 4 types of troops, 2 fortification types and 2 support types. Our consultant, Boris Yulin, carefully studied the historical details. 

Commander specialisations are based on the real battles they took part in, on the tactical techniques and unit types they used. 
As the loyalty level of your units increases, so will their level of competency. 
Currently, working to earn your commanders’ loyalty gets you units when you reach Level 3. As part of the reward system rebalancing you will also get units on the first two levels. When hovering over a unit, you'll see the level it is available at displayed. 

At the beginning of this entry we lifted the veil and told you about our plans to introduce new commanders. We are going to add one for each nation.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/29/claude.jpg[/img]

Please welcome new commander , Sir Claude Auchinleck, a British military commander and Field Marshal. When the war broke out, he was the commander of the Army in Narvik during the Norwegian campaign (April-June 1940). After that he was appointed Commander-in-Chief in India (1940-41), and from the middle of 1941 onward he commanded all of the British forces in North Africa and the Middle East. In our game Sir Claude Auchinleck will be a Commander of Infantry Operations with the corresponding unit assignments.

[b][i]Whom would you like to see on the part of Germany and the USSR?[/i][/b]

We'd like to add a Commander of Artillery and a Commander of Aircraft to the game. Feel free to offer your own suggestions in the comments, and your idea might just be the one we add to the game!

[h1]3. Statistics and Replays[/h1]

[i]This part of the development blog will be definetely interesting for those who haven't checked out the latest updates :)[/i]

Now, when the battle is over, you'll be able to see detailed game statistics in the combat reports. You'll be able to see all important information: player nicknames, battlefields, rewards and a KDA (kill/death/assistance) analog.

Let's consider that last parameter in more detail. 
1.	The Destroyed multiplier will be calculated in supply points instead of unit kills. You'll probably agree, that destroying a Tiger is not as easy as killing a T-70.
2.	Instead of "deaths" you'll be able to see a breakdown of the proportion of your troops you called in during the battle. All in all, you'll be able to calculate your own efficiency by comparing columns 1 and 2. 
3.	You'll also see the amount of damage points you inflicted during the battle.

And one more thing. Before seeing the statistics, you'll also be able to take a look at the awards. Instead of reading about the new screen, just look at it:

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/29/ezgif-789676877.gif[/img] 

[i]Thank you for your kind attention and see you on the battlefield!
We look forward to your commander suggestions! :)[/i]

notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/bum.png[/img]

[h1]Gameplay Changes: [/h1]  [olist]
[*]Added 5 new campaign missions and 2 side-missions for USSR. 
[*]Battle results screen has been redone completely. 
[*]Battle replays which can be accessed from battle results screen have been added to the game.
[*]Reworked commander bonuses; for example, Soviet general Konev will now give heavy tanks bonuses, since USSR did not have a commander who provided buffs for heavy tanks.
[*]You can see all factions’ battle fronts on the globe now.
[*]Updated UI icons for all USSR and German armored vehicles; in upcoming versions other icons will be updated too, including infantry ones as well.
[*]Rewards screen has been updated.
[*]You can now use WASD keys for scrolling on globe screen. It can also be done with mouse. 
[*]You can change your attack commander by clicking on commander’s icon on the screen shown before the battle. 
[*]Increased drop of additional reward, namely fortifications.
[*]Session notification history feature is back; you can now press Ctrl+L to see all messages you’ve received during a mission via radio.[/olist]

[h1]Fixed Issues:[/h1]
[olist]
[*]The error "-2147" that sometimes occurred during matchmaking and could block players from playing skirmish is finally fixed.
[*]Players’ readiness status in PvP modes is now being updated in real time.
[*]Fixed tank firing animations. 
[*]Weapon descriptions for armored vehicles are restored.
[*]Previously, when moving cursor over an object more than once, its name would not be displayed; this issue is fixed now.
[*]Previously, when pausing the game and clicking on any unit, all of the units of the same type would be selected; this is now fixed.
[*]Previously, if several unit squads occupied a building if you wanted any of them to leave it, they left it all at once. Now you can select the one leaving the building, while the others will be left inside.
[*]Removed white message popups that notified about mission replacement.
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause game to freeze during session load.
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented players from calling last unit from reserve.
[*]Re-enabled area bombardment for USA MRL.[/olist]

notes.title: Development Blog #28
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/gif2.gif[/img]

[h1]What's happening right now?[/h1]

Our work on the Soviet campaigns is currently in full swing, but apart from it each studio team member has a lot of things to do. This Development Blog episode will tell you about the work of one of our programmers, who decided to spend some time improving the visual component of Blitzkrieg 3.

Update 0.9.2 brought us a new interface, and some changes in the colour palette of the game with it. Judging from the survey results, many of you liked it. We are going to move forward and polish up the models and animations we have to make the game look better and more spectacular, and at the same time realistic and adequately conveying the atmosphere of the World War II. 

[h1]1. Models and tree shadows[/h1]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/trees.jpg[/img]

Let's consider all the models from left to right (pay attention to both the front and rear views):[list]
[*]The first version correctly depicts the leaves, but doesn’t do a very good job with lighting. 
[*]The second one is good with lighting, but the leaves are darker than they should be in some places. That’s because in real life leaves let some light pass through. 
[*]The third version is the final one. It works correctly with illumination, and the leaves do not absorb all the light hitting them thanks to the semi-transparency effect.[/list]

You'll see the new trees on the Rzhev map!

[h1]2. Explosion and fire effects[/h1]

We are now updating the old effects: they are becoming more detailed and realistic. Animation is getting vibrant new details. Hot air trembling makes the game look more dynamic and realistic. Finally, it just looks spectacular! :)

We'd like to present you some static screenshots and gif files, showing what explosions will look like in the very next version of the game:

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/explosion.jpg[/img]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/whaze.gif[/img][img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/wohaze.gif[/img] 

[h1]3. Landscape matters[/h1]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/change.gif[/img]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/rocks3.jpg[/img]

We softened the seams between landscape and different environment objects by working with shaders. What a trifle, on the face of it, but this feature lets our artists create more colourful and lively landscapes. 

Ivan, our programmer, was so happy that he started applying this filter to everything that moves or stands. The effect looked fine with almost everything, but, course we couldn't quite get by without a hitch. The moment the programmer tried the new technology on horses,  they started looking like horror movie characters. Having buried themselves up to their necks, the horses were looking absently at the one who created them. Ivan saw this nightmare and decided that it's too much. He saved the poor animals, and kept the filter active only for the things that actually needed it.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/horses.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Development Blog #28
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/gif2.gif[/img]

[h1]What's happening right now?[/h1]

Our work on the Soviet campaigns is currently in full swing, but apart from it each studio team member has a lot of things to do. This Development Blog episode will tell you about the work of one of our programmers, who decided to spend some time improving the visual component of Blitzkrieg 3.

Update 0.9.2 brought us a new interface, and some changes in the colour palette of the game with it. Judging from the survey results, many of you liked it. We are going to move forward and polish up the models and animations we have to make the game look better and more spectacular, and at the same time realistic and adequately conveying the atmosphere of the World War II. 

[h1]1. Models and tree shadows[/h1]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/trees.jpg[/img]

Let's consider all the models from left to right (pay attention to both the front and rear views):[list]
[*]The first version correctly depicts the leaves, but doesn’t do a very good job with lighting. 
[*]The second one is good with lighting, but the leaves are darker than they should be in some places. That’s because in real life leaves let some light pass through. 
[*]The third version is the final one. It works correctly with illumination, and the leaves do not absorb all the light hitting them thanks to the semi-transparency effect.[/list]

You'll see the new trees on the Rzhev map!

[h1]2. Explosion and fire effects[/h1]

We are now updating the old effects: they are becoming more detailed and realistic. Animation is getting vibrant new details. Hot air trembling makes the game look more dynamic and realistic. Finally, it just looks spectacular! :)

We'd like to present you some static screenshots and gif files, showing what explosions will look like in the very next version of the game:

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/explosion.jpg[/img]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/whaze.gif[/img][img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/wohaze.gif[/img] 

[h1]3. Landscape matters[/h1]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/change.gif[/img]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/rocks3.jpg[/img]

We softened the seams between landscape and different environment objects by working with shaders. What a trifle, on the face of it, but this feature lets our artists create more colourful and lively landscapes. 

Ivan, our programmer, was so happy that he started applying this filter to everything that moves or stands. The effect looked fine with almost everything, but, course we couldn't quite get by without a hitch. The moment the programmer tried the new technology on horses,  they started looking like horror movie characters. Having buried themselves up to their necks, the horses were looking absently at the one who created them. Ivan saw this nightmare and decided that it's too much. He saved the poor animals, and kept the filter active only for the things that actually needed it.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/horses.jpg[/img]

Apart from the seams, we also have a completely re-worked toolbox for creating... grass!
Map decoration now takes less time, and the result is better.
The screenshots show the effects "before" and "after", both in the editor and on game maps: in Luga and at one of the multiplayer bases.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/gra.jpg[/img]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/grass.jpg[/img]

We also added a softness effect to particles: let's have a look at a clear illustration to see what it changes. 
On the first picture, the border between landscape and smoke is clearly visible. The second picture shows the smoke creeping softly along the ground. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/28/boom.jpg[/img]

Officers, this is just a tiny part of what is going to change in the game. You'll see the results of all this work in battle soon!

[i]See you on the battlefield![/i]

notes.content:

[h1]FIXED ISSUES:[/h1][olist]
[*]Fixed several cases when players would get disconnected from the server, including disconnects happening at the end of the missions.

[*]Horizontal scrolling errors have been fixed.
[*]Infantry units which are holding their positions in fortifications are now shown on the central panel (same as infantry units in buildings).

[*]Units, which were shown without weapons during cut-scenes, now have their them in the right place. 
[*]Now, after their elimination, infantry units are not falling from the fog of war. 
[*]Fixed several cases when tank pillbox/trench construction timers were displayed incorrectly.
[*]Infantry received during the battle wasn't able to dig trenches. This bug has been fixed.
[*]PvP mode selection is now saved across game sessions.
[*]Fixed several cases when central panel would sort units incorrectly.[/olist]

[h1]KNOWN ISSUES:[/h1][olist]
[*]An enemy’s infantryman can move separately from the rest of his squad (it will be fixed in the next version of the game).
[*]There are still some errors left in a few side missions' awards descriptions.
[/olist]

notes.title: Development Blog #27
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/ezgif.com-resize%20(4).gif[/img]

[h1]What’s happening right now?[/h1]

Work on the Soviet and Allied campaigns is currently in full swing. Patch 0.9.2 is already bringing you the first playable Soviet mission: The Luga Line. The rest of the campaign will follow very soon. 
For now, we’re going to tell you about the battles you’ll take part in if you choose the Allied side.

[h1]1. The Libyan Operation [/h1]

In September 1940, Italian forces under the command of Rodolfo Graziani invaded British-controlled Egypt. However, after advancing only a few dozen kilometres into the country, the Italians stopped their offensive and set up camp.
Despite being clearly outnumbered—36,000 Allied troops against 150,000 on the Italian side—the British commander Archibald Wavell decided to strike with full force at the enemy forces. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/1.jpg[/img]

Your objective is to capture the Italian HQ, thereby changing the course of the war.

[h1]2. The Battle of Crete. Operation Mercury[/h1]

In order to establish complete strategic control over the Mediterranean Basin and definitively drive Allied forces out from it, the German command decided to occupy Crete. 
However, it proved unassailable: the British navy was in full control of the coastal waters, while a garrison of 42,000 Allied troops had been stationed on the island itself. To break through the defences, the Germans decided to conduct a large-scale airborne operation. 
Despite heavy losses, Hitler’s army succeeded in its plan. Chances to save the civilians, as well as some of the troops, are extremely small. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/2.jpg[/img]

You will be tasked with evacuating staff officers and AA gunners from an airport that has been captured by the Germans. Remember that a fierce battle is being fought all around you, so you must act with extreme caution! Your intervention is the only chance to preserve the lives of at least some of the troops on the island.

[h1]3. The Relief of Tobruk. Operation Crusader[/h1]

In March 1941, German troops under the command of Erwin Rommel routed the British and drove them out of Libya. The British garrison in Tobruk found itself under siege.

The first attempt at relieving the siege was unsuccessful. After meticulous preparations, British forces conducted another offensive on the 18th of November, but failed to achieve victory again. On the 21st of November, Rommel counterattacked and tried to seize the initiative. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/3.jpg[/img]

You will be tasked with conducting a difficult but important operation. In order to break the string of defeats, German forces must be cut off from their reserves—or the Allied armies will be reduced to mere handfuls of soldiers. The Germans are persistently attacking the 4th Indian Division, and chances of victory are diminishing by the day. If you manage to deny fuel to the enemy, the Allied forces will be able to continue their attack and liberate the besieged Tobruk.

[h1]4. El Alamein. Operation Lightfoot[/h1]

In the summer of 1942, Erwin Rommel pushed the British forces back into Egypt and captured Tobruk. However, subsequent action at El Alamein came to a positional dead end. Neither the Germans nor the British were able to breach each other’s defences. 
In October 1942, the Allies began their second offensive. They were unsuccessful despite extremely heavy fighting, while Rommel was forced to abandon his positions and retreat, having lost his vehicles and run out of fuel and ammunition.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/4.jpg[/img]

Although on the retreat, the German forces continue to pose an enormous threat. In order to ensure the safety of the Allied forces, you must strike at the airfield used by the enemy airforce. Your courageous actions on the battlefield will help consolidate the position at El Alamein. The only path towards the airfield lies through the Qattara Depression, considered impassable. In the course of the operation, you will face superior German numbers, and only the careful, well considered selection of tactics will help you achieve your objective. 

[h1]5. The Battle of Anzio[/h1]

Unable to breach the Gustav Line, the Allies were stalled at Monte Cassino. The determination was made that the defences could only be breached by attacking from the sea.
The Allied army must land at Anzio and make a risky attempt to overpower the German forces. However, this order cannot be executed without help from you. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/5.jpg[/img]

The enemy’s attention must be distracted from the landing, or the operation will fail. Several Allied units will assist you in creating a diversion. Once the bulk of the army lands successfully, you will have to evacuate the remaining troops under your command from the battle zone. 

[h1]6. The Normandy Landings. Operation Overlord [/h1]

In the summer of 1944, the Allies began the largest amphibious operation in history, opening the Second Front in Europe. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/6.jpg[/img]

Among the first to arrive at the scene of the action —the Atlantic Wall—are your troops. You will be in charge of ensuring a successful start to the operation. 
The German coastal battery is a serious threat to Allied troops. You must not only capture it, but also hold it while the enemy does all they can to breach your defences, which are blocking the way towards a strategically important point. 

[h1]7. The Siege of Bastogne [/h1]

In 1944, the German command made its last attempt to turn the tide of the war. For this purpose, they struck at Ardennes, where aircraft had been grounded due to prolonged bad weather. The Allied front wasn’t prepared for the attack. The Germans advanced 70 kilometres, winning victory after victory. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/27/71.jpg[/img]

The Allied armies are on the verge of panic. The situation is difficult indeed. It’s urgent to restore the soldiers’ morale!

With support from heavy vehicles, you will have to prevent German acts of sabotage and contact the American paratroopers holding the town. Help the Allied forces stop the German offensive.

[i]See you on the battlefield![/i]

notes.title: Update 0.9.2
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/26/ezgif-3230489965.gif[/img]

[h1]Gameplay Changes:[/h1]		[olist]	
[*]All infantry units except snipers are now able to dig trenches. Taking damage or receiving different orders interrupts the digging process.
[*]All armoured vehicles now have the Dig In ability. A unit cannot attack while digging in. Taking damage does not interrupt the process.		
[*]A new mission from the Soviet campaign, The Luga Line, has been added to the game.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/26/prew_luga_3.png[/img]

[i]In the early stages of the war, the Soviet army was not faring well. Advancing on the German left flank, Army Group North routed the North-Western Front and was already closely approaching Leningrad by the third week of the war. At that point, however, they were stopped at the newly created Luga defensive line. The Germans were stuck there for a month and a half. They were never able to breach the line and eventually flanked it.
You will be tasked with conducting a special operation in the rear to destroy the anti-aircraft cover and hold back the enemy's counteroffensive until reinforcements arrive.[/i]

[*]The commander system has been reintroduced to the game. A number of changes have been made to it. A commander can strengthen some of your troops. Rewards can be earned by raising each commander's loyalty level.
[*]Leaderboards have been reintroduced to the game. These are available through the menu, or by clicking Rankings in the upper left corner.
[*]The reward system for side missions has been changed; you will now receive the units listed in the mission description upon first completion. 	
[*]The provisional shop has been removed from the game. Players who haven't made any purchases in it will get a minimum set of essential units.
[*]The combat and base interfaces have gotten a significant visual overhaul.
[*]The globe's appearance has been changed, and new icons added.	
[*]Owners of the Deluxe and Strategic editions of the game have gotten their statues back.
[*]The March on Daugavpils mission has been significantly simplified.	[/olist]	
		
[h1]Fixed Issues:	[/h1]	[olist]		
[*]Fixed the freezes that previously affected all side missions, most notably the Essential Provisions side mission.			
[*]Turning on vertical sync no longer causes a frame rate drop.
[*]Fixed freezes occurring when the opponent calls in new troops.	
[*]Removed a delay in the interface response to pressing buttons.
[*]Fixed a bug causing players to stop receiving support points mid-combat during a skirmish.	
[*]Corrected historical inaccuracies on some of the commander portraits.
[*]Fixed a bug in the Large Calibre side-mission whereby completing the task to eliminate gun crews would fail to register.	
[*]Fixed a bug in the March on Daugavpils mission whereby reinforcements could not be requested despite available reserve troops and sufficient support points.	
[*]Added missing unit tooltips in the pre-battle window.			[/olist]

[h1]Known Issues:	[/h1]		[olist=1]	
[*]Functionality for assessing a commander's bonuses is yet to be implemented.	
[*]Incorrect shell explosion effects above trenches.
[*]Mouse-wheel scrolling does not work when viewing statistics and in matches’ results.
[*]Puddles may incorrectly display on top of trenches.	
[*]A white square will appear instead of the image in the pop-out message if you click on missions that are not implemented in the game yet. 
[*]Menu will not pop out after you cancel PvP search (it will show up after you open any mission up). 
[*]Pillboxes’ timers work incorrectly.
[*]Slots for infantry in fortifications are not always shown.
[*]The progress of assaulting houses is not shown.
[*]If you own a low-spec PC, you may face some issues with FPS in Luga (first Soviet mission).
	[/olist]

notes.title: Development Blog #26
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/26/ezgif-2969252073.gif[/img]

[h1]Dear commanders, today in our development blog:[/h1][list]
[*]We'll tell you how to vote in the Steam survey;
[*]We'll share good news about the encyclopedia;
[*]We'll look into some important aspects of the game;
[*]And we'll tell you about some tweaks and features in the next version (a complete list of changes is coming soon). [/list]

[h1]About the Survey[/h1]
We added a survey to the game a week ago, and its findings may influence the development process. Unfortunately, the survey hasn’t been appearing right after first entering the game, as it was supposed to. We'll definitely fix it, [b]for now you can vote by clicking "News" in the top left corner of the screen on the globe. [/b]
Please let us know what you think about our project and give your vote!

[h1]About the Encyclopedia[/h1]
Many players have really liked the Blitzkrieg 2 encyclopedia. But when we announced its analogue in Blitzkrieg 3, some didn't like our idea to publish the encyclopedia on the website.
Well, we have good news for you! :)
We've decided to add this important component in-game. The encyclopedia will provide you with the historical background and detailed game characteristics of the units, and just as importantly will help you find out where to find the particular types of troops or vehicles you need. This information will enable you to approach any battle tactically and deliberately. 

[h1]Important Notes[/h1][list]
[*]There are only a few players who know that successfully positioned defence, impenetrable to the enemy, may grant you troops in amounts comparable to Skirmish rewards. This is a great reason to use all of your knowledge when placing your units, guns and pillboxes at your base. Just imagine: you go to bed, wake up, enter the game in the evening, and there they are: two new Tigers on the Units panel! 
[*]Last time we announced in the development blog that we would add an opportunity to wipe progress on your own to the menu. This option will be activated with the release of the Soviet campaign. You'll be able to wipe individual factions, as well as all at once. 
[*]You often ask us how to change your faction in the game. To change factions, enter your base, press ESC and then choose the menu item you need.
[*]We have received multiple complaints that it is impossible to place anything on the parade ground of the base, which is against common sense and tactics. We are working on it now.[/list]

[h1]About the Upcoming Update (complete list of tweaks and innovations coming soon)[/h1][list]
[*]Lags in side missions has been fixed.
[*]Essential Provisions mission: trucks do not have such a huge amount of health anymore.
[*]Large Caliber mission: we've fixed the bug making the mission not count as complete, even if you meet all requirements (nothing happened after clearing the guns).
[*]The provision points bug in Skirmish has been fixed.
[*]The bug causing doubled units has been fixed.
[*]Having analysed the statistics of mission completions, we've come to the conclusion that Daugavpils has become a stumbling block for many players. Therefore we've made its completion a bit easier.
[*]We will be adding a Depth of Field option to the game. This will let you make fascinating screenshots, but we recommend not using this option in PvP. This option defocuses the landscape around your unit. While that makes for very compelling imagery, it gets in the way during battle. [/list]

[i]See you on the battlefield![/i]

notes.title: Development Blog #25
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/25/ezgif-2278065464cr.gif[/img]

[h1]What’s happening right now?[/h1]

Greetings, dear commanders! Today we are going to answer several pressing questions, dot the “i’s” and cross the “t’s” in the next update, explain certain development trends, and, of course, find out what you think of all this!

[h1]On the agenda:[/h1]
1) Changes in the commander system
2) Changes in the drop system
3) Bonuses in the game’s Deluxe Version
4) The new interface

Let’s begin!

[h1]Changes in the Commander System[/h1][list]
[*]As you may remember, we decided to abandon the commander upgrade system completely. Now you don’t need to level up your commanders but you must effectively accomplish combat assignments to earn trust points. 
In PvE, you must complete missions with a certain number of stars for the command to start believing in you. In PvP, you will also be able to prove yourself and earn the respect of the General HQ.
[*]Commanders will be present both in PvE and PvP starting with the next update. 
We’d like to make our game historically accurate, that’s why they will be strictly bound to missions in PvE: you can only use the commander who actually participated in that operation. 
[*]The commander reward system will become clearer and easier to grasp. A dialogue will appear, showing the trust level that will unlock unit upgrades or some troops for you as rewards. 
[*]We want to introduce a controllable component to the game through the commander system. At their maximum trust level, each commander will give you a one-time bonus of a certain type of troops. This means that if you cannot receive a certain unit as a reward for battles, there is always an alternative. By the way, we plan on implementing only 3 trust levels.
5) You will be able to boost your trust among all commanders available to you. We are not going to limit you with only one of them :)[/list]

[h1]Changes in the Drop System[/h1][list]
[*]We are introducing guaranteed rewards for first-time completion of side missions.
[*]After you complete campaigns, you will have access to a number of units the receipt of which is bound to your ranking. It means that if you make enough progress, you will able to receive troops not available to those who haven’t achieved such results yet.
[*]Right now we are working on adjusting the drop system, and your feedback can influence those changes. We want the rewards for your victories to be clear and desired. [/list]

[h1]Bonuses of the Game’s Deluxe Version[/h1]
Many players have asked what happened to the rewards that were received when you bought the Deluxe Version.[list]
[*]When they progress through missions, owners of the Deluxe Editions will be able to obtain unique units in addition to the usual rewards.
[*]The statue hasn‘t been forgotten, either. It will definitely be back! [/list]

[h1]The New Interface[/h1]
Although the interface was updated in Version 0.9, many players didn’t like it as it was too difficult, ponderous, and awkward... 
We appreciate your opinions, and taking them into account, we started a redesign.
Here is the result of our work. We did our best to lighten the visual component, make panels more attractive, change the design of icons and frontline borders. 
Please tell us how you like our new design :)

[i](to see the pictures in bigger resolution, click using the right mouse button on them and select the first option from the top)[/i]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/25/central_panel_battle_screen_base.png[/img]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/25/central_panel_globus.png[/img]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/25/central_panel_globus_brief_scroll.png[/img]

[i]Dear firends, please pay attention that these are screenshots from the development progress and not everything you may see on them will make it to the final cut![/i]

[h1]Some important notes:[/h1][list]
[*]Dear officers, many of you asked us to add an option to remove the interface from the screen. Now you can do so by pressing the F10 button.
[*]Some players complained that trucks in “Essential Provisions” were tough as tanks. We have fixed that bug. Now it will be much easier to destroy the trucks.
[*]We haven’t forgotten about other important game components. Now we are working on both the USSR campaign and on the multiplayer. Among other things, Custom Game, an option to play Skirmishes in a group with your friends. 
[*]We’ll organise a mass account wipe closer to the game release. 
[*]In the next updates, you will be able to reset the game progress on your own. This option will appear in the menu. 
[*]In 0.9.2 update we are going to return the commander system. 
[*]Statistics will appear again in the next update.[/list]

[i]See you on the battlefield![/i]

notes.title: Development Blog #24
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/24/ezgif-2846871951.gif[/img]

[h1]What’s happening right now?[/h1]

Since the release of the German campaign, we’ve been fully engrossed in developing missions for the USSR. There will be 16 of them in total: 7 main missions and 9 side missions. Players who’ve been following the project’s progress since its inception probably already have a good idea of the kind of missions we’ve got in store for you. In this dev blog, besides a brief introduction of the missions, we’d like to talk about some of the highlights of the Soviet campaign that we find interesting, as well as several aspects planned for the game’s future development.

[h1]A word about the Soviet Campaign[/h1]

We’ve been very meticulous about choosing the most significant events of World War II that we’d like to include in the USSR campaign. With guidance from our historical consultant, Boris Yulin, we came up with the following list of battles:
[list]
[*][b]The Luga Line[/b]
[*][b]The Rzhev–Vyazma Operation[/b]
[*][b]Sevastopol[/b]
[*][b]Stalingrad[/b]

[img]http://турист.рф/upload/iblock/fd0/fd056491c32f3876aedcd4b4289885d9.jpg[/img]

The main events of the Battle of Stalingrad will unfold around [i][b]Pavlov’s House[/b][/i]. This residential building became a veritable fortress for Soviet soldiers in 1942; despite being outnumbered, they defended it for 58 days. A small group of soldiers (different sources put the number between 24 and 31) managed to survive mortar fire, artillery shelling, and aerial bombardment. These events have entered the history of the war as an epitome of the Soviet army’s endurance and valour.

[*][b]The Battle of Kursk[/b]
[*][b]Warsaw. Operation Bagration[/b]

[img]http://worldoftanks.ru/dcont/fb/uncommon_images/history_section/bagration/1508.jpg?MEDIA_PREFIX=/dcont/fb/[/img]

Operation Bagration was the largest-scale military operation conducted by the Soviet command in World War II. In the game, your group, supported by heavy armament fire and army troops, must battle through to the west bank of the Vistula and establish contact with the Polish rebels. The primary objective  is to find, among several of their groups, the one that has members of the command in it. 
 
[*][b]The Fall of Berlin[/b]

[img]http://smartnews.ru/storage/c/2013/04/19/1366378218_661757_10.jpg[/img]

The Battle of Berlin was the largest military offensive in all of humanity’s history. An immense number of soldiers took part in it: based on the size of the German capital at the time, one could put their count at no less than 400 men per house. The city was swarming with infantry and military equipment; ambushes were easy to lay on its narrow streets.
This colossal battle simply cannot be omitted. As the commander of the special forces, you’ll be in charge of important assignments on the road to Berlin, aimed at alleviating the toll the offensive is taking. If you successfully complete the mission, soldiers from your detachment who’ve distinguished themselves in battle will be given the honour of raising the flag over the Reichstag.
[/list]

[h1]On Changes to the Game[/h1]

After a careful analysis of player feedback on the German campaign, we’ve decided to change a few things about the game. We’ll also keep that feedback in mind while working on the USSR missions. 
We realised that our missions currently restrict the player’s actions to a greater degree than we’d originally intended. We’re planning to: 

[i]1) give the player more freedom of action; [/i]
At the moment, players only have a limited choice of available strategies. That’s something we’d like to fix, giving you options to complete objectives by any means available within a particular mission’s context. 
To illustrate the specifics of combat, let us consider the situation in Stalingrad:
An example of urban warfare, this battle’s decisive features included:
- close combat inside buildings;
- narrow passages and barricades providing ample opportunities for ambushes.
In a situation like this, a comprehensive approach to storming the streets is the key to victory. For instance, the Soviet army was using the "Herringbone" technique. Tanks followed the infantry on opposite sides of the street, eliminating enemies. Knowing of the limited range of the German Faustpatrone, the tanks kept a distance of at least 150 metres from buildings at all times, firing at the enemy from long range. Assault parties then burst into houses and established positions inside. Once consolidated, the infantry threw smoke grenades from the windows so that the main forces could pass by unnoticed. This coordinated effort by tanks and assault squads was instrumental in the successful accomplishment of combat assignments.

[i]2) clearly indicate key clues to efficient mission completion; [/i]
We heard back from many players who felt the Axis campaign was too hard. After a careful analysis, we’ve concluded that the game currently doesn’t provide clear enough clues to efficient mission completion. We’re taking this factor into account while working on the Soviet campaign, which will be more explicit in pointing to the optimal methods of completing combat assignments.

[i]3) highlight the characteristics of individual battles;  [/i]
For instance, in the battle of Sevastopol, the Germans fielded an enormous amount of weaponry, including 2 self-propelled Karl-Gerät mortars and the unique ultraheavy Dora railway gun. On their approach to the city, the Nazis spent what would normally be two months’ supply of ammunition in a single day. For its part, the Soviet command used coastal artillery for defence. Both sides of the conflict were banking on a particular type of armament, and we want the game to better reflect that.

[i]4) take into account the real-life commanders’ strategies in our mission design.[/i]
For instance, Admiral Oktyabrsky would often rely on highly mobile contingency corps, such as assault infantry, marines, or medium tanks. 

We hope you’ve found today’s Dev Blog interesting!
See you on the battlefield!

notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/23/ezgif-3350566837.gif[/img]

[h1]What’s happening right now?[/h1]

It was quite recently that we released Update 0.9, radically changing some aspects of the game. Now we are polishing this version, analysing your feedback, and fixing bugs.

We urge you to be active and report on any issues to the support HQ at support@blitzkrieg.com, and share your thoughts and suggestions in all social networks. Not a single message will remain unnoticed :)

Today’s Developer Diaries will be short but sweet. We will tell you about spectators, the vehicle camouflage colour selection system, and heroic units.

[b]Spectators[/b]
First, we would like to explain what a spectator is. It is a person who is present in the game but does not directly participate. 

Steam has a Watch Game feature similar to what we are going to implement. But we plan to give you more freedom. You will be able not only to look at a battle from a player’s position, but to move freely on the battleground. Thus, you are given an opportunity to watch an ongoing battle, moving freely on the map and not losing sight of a single maneuver.

[b]Vehicle Camouflage Colour Patterns[/b]
Tank camouflage colours not suitable for missions performed in the conditions that the army finds themselves in have become a sore problem in the Blitzkrieg 3 game community.An illustrative example is North Africa, where tanks with standard armor colors cut through the sand dunes. 

We are going to implement a system that will automatically replace the vehicle colours with those matching the climatic conditions. This will allow you to experience the game as something more serious and realistic. 

[b]Heroic Units[/b]
We introduced the rarity system in Update 0.9 of the game. In following versions, we plan to add another type of units, which will be called “heroic”. These troops will be the rarest and the most powerful in the whole game, so getting them won’t be easy.

We only plan a small number of such squads, maybe 1 or 2 per faction. These units are unique: they will speak their own audio lines when performing actions, and they will have individual animations. 

At present we are still thinking over the list of historical personalities that will become heroic units. We have a lot of ideas, but we’ll have to exclude some of them before we present for your judgment the update implementing the rarity system.

You can offer your candidates to become heroic units in the game! We will make note of your ideas :) 

For example, one suitable historical figures is Zinoviy Kolobanov, whose crew destroyed 22 tanks in 30 minutes during the Kingisepp-Luga Defensive Operation.  

See you on the battlefield, officers!

notes.title: Update 0.9
notes.content:
[img]http://s019.radikal.ru/i615/1608/b8/18a0ae588ef3.gif[/img]

Commanders, we would like to invite you to try this wide-ranging update full of exciting changes: a campaign on behalf of the Axis countries, a modified economy, a rarity system, and a temporary store.

The General Staff urges you to promptly report all errors and inaccuracies you encounter in combat. Contribute to the project’s development and help it improve even more!

[h1]What’s new?[/h1]
[list][*][b]A full-blown German campaign has been added.[/b]
You will have 7 missions that cover the main periods of the war and show the role of special forces in significant operations. We’ve done our best to make them as historically accurate as possible.

[*][b]Two new missions have been added to the campaign: [/b]
The Battle of El Alamein and the Siege of Sevastopol.

[i]The Battle of El Alamein:[/i]
The Panzer Army Africa under Rommel’s command has suffered a defeat against the British, who used their greatly superior forces and air supremacy to break through the German frontlines and start pursuing the enemy troops. The Italian forces that Rommel left without vehicles have been taken prisoner.
The taskforce must attack a British base far behind enemy lines. The goal of the attack is to distract the enemy and deprive it of the supplies it needs for an offensive. The taskforce can count on any assistance from the remaining German forces.

[i]The Siege of Sevastopol:[/i]
The 11th Army under Manstein’s command has received an order to take Sevastopol at any cost. A significant number of Luftwaffe forces and unlimited ammo have been supplied to complete the objective.
Supported by heavy vehicles, your taskforce has to break through to the shore of Severnaya Bay and ensure fire adjustment for the siege artillery on the mooring areas to prevent the Soviet command from transferring ammunition and reinforcements to Sevastopol.

[*][b]9 secondary missions have been added.[/b]
In addition to key campaign missions, some extra PvE battles will be available. You will receive rewards for your victories and be able to toughen up your troops and commanders in combat and increase their stats.

[*][b]The game’s economic system has been changed.[/b]
You can no longer purchase units for resources (except for the temporary store). You will receive rewards for participating in battles. You will be able to gain access to new vehicles, infantry, weapons, and obstructions during combat. Exactly what depends on the game mode and map.

[*][b]Tiers have been removed from the game.[/b]

[*][b]All player rankings will be reset [/b]and divided for different modes. No leaderboard is available in the current version, but this is temporary.

[*]You will not lose your previous progress: you will immediately go to the corresponding war period (starting from this version it will divided into 3 eras). However, you will lose all vehicles, infantry, and obstructions and have to assemble your army again. [b]For a limited time only, a store been added to the game[/b] where you can buy various units for a temporary currency. You will get a certain number of glory points depending on your progress, tier, and rank in the record table.

[*][b]The main menu has been removed from the game.[/b]

[*]New players now choose a faction immediately and start the game with the Poland mission. When they log in next time, they are immediately transferred to the [b]global map[/b]. This window will show all available battles, transfers to the base and between eras, a player’s army, the system menu, news, etc. All stores have been removed from your combat section. A parade ground where your vehicles will be shown has been added. The appearance of the base will reflect your progress and correspond to the historical era.

[*]Now, before entering any battle (including a single-user PvE),[b] a player assembles a detachment from the vehicles and infantry at their disposal.[/b] Units taken into combat must suit the conditions of the historical operation (in terms of years and purpose). Part of the detachment can be available when the battle starts, while the remainder can be available later, for use as reinforcements.

[*][b]Many changes have been made in the balance for the Skirmish and Assault modes, including [/b] alterations to attack limits and generating Reinforcement Points and Victory Points. General combat stats for vehicles have also been recalculated, including side/rear damage, aiming time, accuracy at close range etc.

[*][b]The total number of units has almost doubled.[/b]

[*]The commander system and chat will be [i]temporarily[/i] unavailable. Also, since the trench system is being reworked, there are no trenches at bases for now.

[*][b]To change faction[/b] in this version of the game, you need to go to your base. While being on it, press ESC and choose the necessary option in the menu.

[*]If you are tier 1 or 2, you will have to replay the first mission of the game. If you reached higher tiers, “Capture of Poland” will be completed with 1 star automatically. You will receive a reward for 1 star walkthrough, also.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Blog #22
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/22/ezgif-3074321506.gif[/img]

[h1]Part 1: What’s happening right now?[/h1]

If you have read previous issues of the Developer Diaries, you probably know that we are now actively working on the next update. We've told you a lot about it, so today we're going to introduce you to one of the aspects of the game you are interested in: the editor.
The ability to create user modifications has already become a traditional feature of the Blitzkrieg game series.
In order to see how functional and convenient the scenario editor interface is, our map designer has been using it for a month to create the Siege of Sevastopol mission. As he was working, he analysed all the editor functions available and came to the conclusion that it lacks some critical capabilities. To keep players from facing the same problem, we are working hard to improve the editor.
As for that mission, you'll be able to check it out very soon, as soon as update 0.9 is released.
Let us know if you like it! :)

To heighten your interest, we've decided to draw back the curtain a bit. Look at this screenshot, and then at this key (which describes each item in the screenshot). 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/22/Screenshot_82.png[/img]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/22/Screenshot_83.png[/img]

[i]What do the numbers and arrows on the editor screenshot mean?[/i]
1. Blueprint start: the blueprint allows you to focus on creating logic without needing to worry about syntax and other aspects of programming languages. But in any case it is important to understand what a variable type, boolean value, method, or loop is if you want to make something more complex than just moving a unit from A to B;
2. The blueprint has determined that the player's units are present in a given sector;
3. An additional blueprint is launched to calculate the average position of the unit in the zone;
4. One of the coast artillery batteries has been ordered to engage fire on the player's units. 

This schematic shows the logic of coast artillery tower behaviour:

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/22/Screenshot_84.png[/img]

As you see, our work on the new visual interface is in full swing. In the future we will actually use it to create all of our new maps and scenarios. We hope you'll like them! 

[h1]Part 2: “Player Suggestions”[/h1]

In anticipation of your questions on the players' editor, we'd like to share our thoughts on it with you. 
There are several reasons why we are not yet able to provide an editor to mode creators. First, we have to separate the editor from the engine. Another thing we have to do is make it possible to work with videos, maps, unit locations, and unit settings in the editor. 
We are planning to create a separate application for making new scenarios. 
The editor allows you to create new maps and change the characteristics of units and some textures as desired. After the game is released we will enable mod support via the Steam Workshop.

See you on the battlefield, officers!
