notes.title: Development Blog #21
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/2_4.gif[/img]

[h1]Part 1: What’s happening right now?[/h1]

The developers of Blitzkrieg 3 will soon bring you Version 0.9, which is designed to integrate all of the game’s elements. We told you about some innovations in previous devblogs, and now it’s time for you to know about them in more detail. Today’s episode of the Developer Diaries will explain how difficult it was for the team to prepare this version, what objectives we had in mind, what we had to abandon, and what made our programmers stay awake for days on end.

[b]More on the Campaign and Additional Missions[/b]

When creating the campaign, we wanted to build an integrated story and tell you about key milestones in the war for the Axis countries. It was equally important for us to emphasise the heroism of ordinary soldiers, their bravery, and their contribution to the common cause. We turned to Boris Yulin, a military historian, to help us make the missions as realistic as possible. Boris has firsthand knowledge of the Blitzkrieg game series, as he helped develop the very first one. This time he personally chose missions for the campaign, as well as sharing his extensive factual knowledge with us.
We couldn’t overlook other battles in World War II. In addition to the 7 main campaign missions, you can also look forward to 9 additional ones. We’ve tried to make them as historically accurate as we can. During combat missions, you will only be able to use and get as a reward units and military hardware that existed in that time period.

[b]New Economy and Counter System[/b]

It’s not easy to implement a new economic system. We needed to rethink and rework a lot of things. We completely dismantled the counter system and then put it back together again from scratch.
We couldn’t introduce any vehicles or units into the game before without greatly affecting the balance. When we introduced the rarity system, it helped us get rid of a number of issues and also make the combat system more varied.

[b]UX/UI[/b]

[i]Konstantin Verbitsky, Senior UX/UI Designer[/i]
“We’ve spent six months working on the version that you’re going to see very soon. As well as carrying out minor updates, we were creating a completely new product. We had to make a lot of changes: some things in the game were inconsistent and badly represented, and some screens looked too bulky. We’ve made all UI elements simpler, and now information is displayed in the right amount just when you need it. Now you can see the backbone of what we’ve been working on. All the screens will get more detailed in the versions to come. When you look at the screenshots, you can check out how many changes we made on a single screen. This is the global map screen, where you will receive information on your progress and success.”

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/ac3723a767e54061e796927c67c84549.png[/img]

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/b3%202016-08-10%2013-46-17-40.jpg[/img]

We’ve changed the look of the screens, added new icons and developed an artistic solution to the rarity system. The game looks really different now. We hope that you’ll like the final result!

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/055593af004641e1aef8c7f3d8da7e2a.png[/img]

[b]Programming[/b]

Our employees focused a great deal of their efforts on adding the trench system in this version. It turned out to be harder than we thought. To give you an insight into the difficulties involved, here are some comments from Artyom Pavlenko, our senior programmer:

[i]What are trenches from a player’s point of view?[/i]
Just holes in the ground that an infantryman jumps into and runs around in...

[i]But what are they from a programmer’s point of view?[/i]
A separate world with its own traversable map and pushout system. When a unit enters this world, they go through special teleportation channels formed just as their path is generated. At this point the unit becomes amorphous, and their physical body doesn’t exist in either world. At the same time, their prototype continues to encounter other units in the external world. When their amorphous body reaches the other world, their physical prototypes gets teleported into the trench to interact with the bodies that are only located in that trench. Sometimes the teleportation fails, and they end up in an untraversable area, a free zone in the external world. This results in the cataclysm of a misplaced unit existing in the external world...

We apologise that you will have to wait a little while longer for the trench system. To keep your spirits up in the meantime, please take a look at the results of our programmers’ work. The code has made it possible for tanks to go through trenches and for infantry to run under vehicles standing above trenches.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/1_1.gif[/img][img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/1_2.gif[/img]

[h1]Part 2: “Player Suggestions”[/h1]

[b]Tedo80 (Steam): [/b]
Will this game have medals and ranks like previous games in the series?

We intend to introduce an achievements system.
You will receive them as you go through the tutorial and make progress for winning battles in a certain way and successfully performing difficult tasks with individual units. For example, destroying a certain number of troops with strike aircraft or maintaining control over all the howitzers on the map.
We don’t have any other plans about similar incentives right now.

[h1]Part 3: “Coming up...”[/h1]

Our upcoming plan is to analyse your feedback to improve the game and make it more interesting. The contents of the next episode of the Developer Diaries will directly depend on your response to this version.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/1_1.gif[/img][img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/21/1_2.gif[/img]

[h1]Part 2: “Player Suggestions”[/h1]

[b]Tedo80 (Steam): [/b]
Will this game have medals and ranks like previous games in the series?

We intend to introduce an achievements system.
You will receive them as you go through the tutorial and make progress for winning battles in a certain way and successfully performing difficult tasks with individual units. For example, destroying a certain number of troops with strike aircraft or maintaining control over all the howitzers on the map.
We don’t have any other plans about similar incentives right now.

notes.title: Development Blog #20
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/b3d33ca0ad2dd6a812be34e97c84e4041916e732.jpg[/img]

[h1]Part 1: What’s happening right now?[/h1]

Work on update 0.9 is going full blast. The purpose of this developer diary is to acquaint you a little more thoroughly with the latest version of the game.

[b]In today's post:[/b]
1) A little about the update
2) Temporary unit shop
3) Trenches
4) New vehicle models announced
5) Future developments

[h1]A little about the update[/h1]

1) We’ve been hard at work on the latest version and wanted to show you the fruits of our labors as soon as possible. You might have some comments, or you might be looking for flaws in this version. We ask that you take a knowledgeable approach to the situation and tell us about any issues you find. We appreciate all your reports of errors and/or bugs. Help us make the game better! 

2) Update 0.9 introduces a full campaign for the “Axis” countries. However, the historical chronicles and missions available in the deluxe and strategic editions of the game will not be available yet when the new version is released. 

3) Many players would like to know whether or not their progress will be reset when the new economy is introduced.
Our answer: no. There will not be a wipe. 
Why?
We feel like it’s important to save your progress and observe how the new economic model works during various stages of progress in the game. 
If you still want to start the game over again, we can reset any base of your choosing. For example, you could save your progress for the Allies, but wipe the USSR. 
To reset one or all of your bases, email us at support@blitzkrieg.com and enter “wipe” in the subject line.  You’ll need to attach two screenshots to the message: one of your base and one of the leaderboard.

We’re planning to do a full wipe when the game launches. Until then, we aren't going to make these sorts of undertakings mandatory. 

4) Since we’re only launching an “Axis” campaign, we expect that the vast majority of players are going to want to play as that faction. We’re temporarily disabling the ban on attacking members of your own coalition (the priority will still be on attacking members of the opposite coalition). 

[h1]Temporary unit shop[/h1]

We’ve already mentioned several time that we're going to introduce a new economy to the game. 
Because of this, we had to think about how to transfer your progress from the old system to the new one.
In the beginning you will be given a certain number of units. You will earn new squads and vehicles by winning battles. You will be able to purchase units similar to those that can be won in battle at the shop. The shop will only be available for a limited time. Your progress will be transferred into a special currency. You can spend this currency on units, fortifications, and barricades. 

[h1]Trenches[/h1]

You’ve been asking for them!
You’ve been waiting for them!
And your cries have been heard by our team! :)

In update 0.9 you will be able to entrench vehicles just like in the previous games in the series, as well as dig trenches. The introduction of this mechanic will significantly impact combat tactics: you will now be able to prepare to meet the enemy. 

You will only be able to use the new commands in battle (in the future you will also be able to give similar orders at the base).  

[i]Entrenching vehicles[/i]
Once a unit receives your orders, it will take up a firing position. It will dig a trench around itself or place sand bags in front of itself and to the sides. Carrying out this order reduces the damage the vehicle will take, but, needless to say, it will also prevent it from moving.

[i]Entrenching infantry[/i]
The new system allows you to dig a trench wherever you want. All infantry units other than snipers can dig trenches. Trenches are made of segments between which soldiers can move freely. 
If your units are in a trench, their dodge chance is increased, and their damage from AoE attacks is reduced. 
If you manage to kill all the enemy soldiers in a trench, your units can occupy the trench and fight from there. 

Here’s a screenshot of a trench during peacetime (men chatting, snacking and hanging out with women — everything’s normal) and one that’s expecting an enemy attack.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/1ded049bb6880dcdd405f5e35d76f6126c94946a.png[/img]

[h1]Expanded unit roster, new models announced[/h1]

We are proud to announce that the roster of units has been almost doubled. In this edition we will show you another new tank and two news SPGs that will be entering the game. In upcoming updates all the vehicles available in PvE will become available in PvP one way or another. For example, if you get the Maus as a reward for completing a mission, you will be able to deploy it both in the campaign and in multiplayer.

The stars of today’s announcement are:

KW-2
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/0c95e5e77771ad2611f7c928486604ebe98bbe17.jpg[/img]

Wespe
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/e67ce0dc8b3f160866227d783873568e22c768d5.jpg[/img]

M10 Wolverine
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/5c7c913c39d14b94e8d3264a2040a9e32ec48098.jpg[/img]

[h1]In keeping with tradition, let’s hear a few words from the guys from the development team about how the week went.[/h1]

[i]Ivan Loktinov, Programmer[/i]
“When the code doesn't work the way you expected...”

[img]http://s017.radikal.ru/i436/1608/cb/e1e95ae74702.gif[/img]

[i]Danil Dvoryaninov, Junior Producer[/i]
The update schedule for our project reminds me of the Wheel of Samsara. The karma you earned in the last version determines the number of bugs in the next one. I’m doing my best to lead a just work life and break the sinful cycle of rebirth!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/0b792934706c371957940b02d807390c7ea8e8c8.gif[/img]

[i]Vadim Yakovlev, Lead Quality Assurance Specialist[/i]
Here’s an illustration of how bugs jump from one programmer to another:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/c98f304f3cdf668e771c782fdd73081623293c7d.gif[/img]

[h1]Part 2: Future developments[/h1]

In this section we review the most frequently encountered questions/complaints/suggestions and tell you which aspects of the project we're still working on.

[b]1) Tutorial/manual[/b]
We often see requests for an in-game tutorial. We haven’t been ignoring this feedback. The project is still in development. Things are changing all the time. However, the tutorial needs to be exact and practical, so it won’t appear until close to launch.
As soon as the primary goals relating to gameplay, balance, and economy have been met, we’ll start working on it. 

[b]2) Saving your game[/b]
We are planning to add an option to save your game. 
It will only be available in historical missions. 
We’re doing this so you can pick up from where you left off when playing long missions.
This option will be introduced in upcoming updates. 

[b]3) Lobby[/b]
You will be able to create private games soon. You will not earn rewards for winning these battles. 
You will be able to partner up with your friends in the lobbies and predetermine the outcome of the battle together. You will earn units and vehicles for winning matchmaking games with your friends. The units that can only be obtained by beating the campaign will not be among these rewards. 

[b]4) Transferring crews[/b]
In upcoming versions of the game you will be able to transfer your crews from one vehicle (tank, SPG) to another. 
For example, let’s say that during the first phase of the war you have a tank that you used to complete all the missions from this time period and have saved up some experience (it's linked to the crew). 
If you transfer the crew to a vehicle in the second time period, the soldiers will lose a little experience (they’ll have to get used to the new vehicle). Transferring an old crew to tanks in the next time period is better than going into battle with green recruits. The old war dogs will show their worth on the battlefield.

[b]5) Upgrades[/b]
In upcoming updates you will gain access to upgrades (they’re linked to historical periods). As a spec ops commander, you work with the most advanced tech that the regular army doesn't have access to.
When you get an upgrade, it is applied to all the vehicles it can be used with. 
For example, let’s say you get reinforced tank treads. This upgrade will be instantly applied to tanks and SPG’s.

See you in the next blog!

notes.title: Development Blog #19
notes.content:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/18/engl.jpg[/img]

[h1]Part 1: What’s happening right now?[/h1]

After they came back from vacation, the team continues to work arduously on Update 0.9. It will contain many innovations that we are going to introduce to you gradually.
Today, as the title suggests, we will tell you about the historical campaign and side missions: how they are structured and connected. Let’s go!

[h1]Campaign[/h1]

The next game update will contain a full-blown campaign for the Axis countries. You can play as any faction. But you will have to play the campaign for Germany.

You can read about the historical campaign and the new economy system [url=http://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791434118091/announcements/detail/598230758564383462]in one of the previous episodes of the Developer Diaries.[/url]

The PvE aspect of the game in Update 0.9 will represent your progress. 
All missions have been carefully selected and are connected to each other so as to best visibly present progression from one era of the war to another. It was important for us to show the player’s progress as a commander from the beginning of the war to its very end.

Each of these periods will have several missions. To complete each of them successfully, you will need a certain fleet of units which you can collect by completing side missions and participating in PvP battles. Corresponding vehicles are assigned to each time period. As consequence, the rewards that you can receive for completing missions in a given period are strictly tied to historical realities. 

Remember that if you play PvP, for example, for the Soviet Union, you will get Soviet units as a reward. But if you play historical missions for Germany, you can use them: when you are in combat, all units from other faction armies will be converted to German ones. 

[h1]Side Missions[/h1]

Let’s look at side missions in more detail: they will appear on the globe as you progress in the campaign, but, more importantly, completing them is not obligatory and does cause any progression through the eras. You will be able to complete them again at any time. Still, keep in mind that if you reach the end of the war but want to play a mission from the first era, your fleet of units will change to correspond to 1939-41. This system also applies to PvP.

Our team has done their best to make sure side missions are interesting to complete and enjoyable to replay. 
Different conditions will be generated in every mission. 
For example, one of your objectives will be to find and destroy a partisan camp. Its location will be different every time. This means that completing this mission will require a different approach every time. We are also planning to add different difficulty levels for such missions. 

[h1]Commanders’ Trust[/h1]

A new commander trust system awaits you. It will allow you to receive new forces or update existing ones.
If you want to get those bonuses, you need to be effective on the battlefield and attain victories. If you do well, the commander will take note of your accomplishments leading to success in his maneuvers and give you different incentives as time goes by. Thus, you will be able to strengthen the forces subordinate to you. 

Depending on the game mode you choose, the model of the trust system will change. 
Campaign missions will not let you change your commander, so you will only earn trust points with them. This decision has historical grounds. Battle will feature the actual commander who took part in it in reality. 
When you are in PvP, you are given a choice. You can earn trust points for the commander that you have chosen. 

[h1]And now, as ever, a few words from our development team about their current week of work.[/h1]

[b]Dmitry Zubachev, 2D/UI Artist[/b]
[i]I’ve got a lot of work, it’s hot on all fronts. That’s why I kit out with tea, sharp styluses, armed to squeeze Photoshop dry.[/i]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/d6c7993b3f7211fe0536fec80b5240a379647be0.gif[/img]

[b]Andrey Zaytsev, Junior Map Designer[/b]
[i]My brain is all loaded up with the preparation of side missions. We have a great deal of work ahead of us... And we’re really short of hands.[/i]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/9744fc5b47bbf21c6073d1b89aef59f9935f7167.gif[/img]

[h1]Part 2: Player Suggestions[/h1]

Today we are going to discuss Comrade [b]Coelian’s[/b] question (from the official forums for our project). [b]Coelian[/b] asks if the game will include a mission for the Soviet Union in 1944.

Our answer to this very interesting and important question? 
The announcement of the [b]Warsaw[/b] mission.

The mission’s historical background is as follows:
Army Groups Centre and North were defeated during Operation Bagration in the summer of 1944. The Soviet troops had reached the borders of Germany and Warsaw. But by the end of the operation the premature Polish uprising started. The Soviet troops were already exhausted and were not able to continue the offensive. Their rear forces stayed far behind. Nevertheless, desperate attempts were made to help the insurgent Poles.

In this mission you will have to break through the German forces and get in touch with the insurgents. Your main objective is to find and provide a way out for the commanders of Armia Ludowa (the People’s Army).

[h1]Part 3. Coming up...[/h1]

In our next entry we’ll tell you in more detail about the new economy system, the updated UI, changes to the base, and the enlarged fleet of units. 

What do you think, which units will be added to the game? :)
P.S. To keep the excitement going and give you a little extra to discuss, we have this screenshot to offer - a new tank:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/65447802bf95e00cd6489e1b864899eaef698d72.jpg[/img]

Nevertheless, desperate attempts were made to help the insurgent Poles.

In this mission you will have to break through the German forces and get in touch with the insurgents. Your main objective is to find and provide a way out for the commanders of Armia Ludowa (the People’s Army).

[h1]Part 3. Coming up...[/h1]

In our next entry we’ll tell you in more detail about the new economy system, the updated UI, changes to the base, and the enlarged fleet of units. 

What do you think, which units will be added to the game? :)
P.S. To keep the excitement going and give you a little extra to discuss, we have this screenshot to offer - a new tank:

notes.title: Development Blog #17
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/DEV17ENG.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Part 1: What's happening right now?[/h1]

As of this writing, our team is working hard on Update 0.8.7. When it is published, you'll probably already be fighting on the new map for the Skirmish mode, while we'll be doing quality assurance of the update and tracking any critical errors.

After a prolonged forced development march, virtually all of our studio will take a small break before our final rush towards the release. The next two weeks are going to be almost complete radio silence, and this blog will take a break, too.

New issues will be released after our vacation to start the third season of our developer diaries.

[h1]Water[/h1]

Those of you who have already played the Strike in the Ardennes mission and the Vineyards of Sicily, the new Skirmish mode map, have most likely noticed that our water visuals have changed. Ivan, who has been working on this change, has written a quick outline of how the work went.

"Implementation of our long-anticipated 'new water' has surprisingly coincided with the upcoming Steam sale. As a result, a relaxed development process, which mostly consisted of watching ripples on water, turned into fierce arguments between us and the Art Department about the final level of water quality in our game...

The first step was painless: we corrected all the visible seam-like artifacts. But artists are artists, and they can easily keep going in their search for perfection :)

First, we added soft edges to the shores
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water1.jpg[/IMG]

Then, a refraction effect to the water
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water2.jpg[/IMG]

We even started experimenting with reflections at some point, and we found a solution, but for some reason the artists didn't like it
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water3.jpg[/IMG]

When the reflections had finally been properly implemented, I just sat down and started taking screenshots, under the pretence of completing my assigned tasks...
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water4.jpg[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water5.jpg[/IMG]
...along with continually correcting landscape texture artifacts.

[url=http://coub.com/view/b1fx6]I have no words to describe the relief I felt when the final version was finished... [/url].

By the way, the water in the game used to look like this:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water6.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Objects[/h1]

While we are talking about development from the artists' perspective, we can't help mentioning the upcoming map for the historical campaign, El Alamein, which our guys have spent lots of time working on.

As usual, we've prepared a unique set of assets for the mission. Here are some of them:

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog2.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog3.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog5.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog6.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog7.jpg[/IMG]

We get a set of parts, just like Lego pieces, which layout artists then use to make a map.

The El Alamein project manager suggested we show the map later, once the signature minarets are ready, so for now you can just imagine how it will be arranged and what it will look like. The only remark we can make is that the map is big and has a ton of buildings.

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog1.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]And now, as usual, a few words from our development team about their most recent week of work.[/h1]

To cut a long story short, and on behalf of entire team:	[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/giphy1.gif[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/giphy2.gif[/IMG]

[h1]Teil 2: „Vorschläge der Spieler“[/h1]

[b]Aleksandr Vitsyn[/b] (Project page on VK): [i]"It's better to replace those 4 game mode buttons with just 1. Or you could just keep adding them and end up filling the entire screen. [On the buttons at the top of the screen]".[/i]

We will come up with a solution for this in one of the next few updates. You will be able to choose multiplayer battles on the "globe" by marking the modes you are interested in and then starting an opponent search. Everything will be more consistent, more convenient, and more attractive.

[h1]Part 3: The Next Episode[/h1]

We'll probably tell you about the next update, but who knows? It will be a new blog season, after all ;)

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water3.jpg[/IMG]

When the reflections had finally been properly implemented, I just sat down and started taking screenshots, under the pretence of completing my assigned tasks...
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water4.jpg[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water5.jpg[/IMG]
...along with continually correcting landscape texture artifacts.

[url=http://coub.com/view/b1fx6]I have no words to describe the relief I felt when the final version was finished... [/url].

By the way, the water in the game used to look like this:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/water6.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Objects[/h1]

While we are talking about development from the artists' perspective, we can't help mentioning the upcoming map for the historical campaign, El Alamein, which our guys have spent lots of time working on.

As usual, we've prepared a unique set of assets for the mission. Here are some of them:

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog2.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog3.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog5.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog6.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog7.jpg[/IMG]

We get a set of parts, just like Lego pieces, which layout artists then use to make a map.

The El Alamein project manager suggested we show the map later, once the signature minarets are ready, so for now you can just imagine how it will be arranged and what it will look like. The only remark we can make is that the map is big and has a ton of buildings.

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/inblog1.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]And now, as usual, a few words from our development team about their most recent week of work.[/h1]

To cut a long story short, and on behalf of entire team:	[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/giphy1.gif[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/17/giphy2.gif[/IMG]

[h1]Teil 2: „Vorschläge der Spieler“[/h1]

[b]Aleksandr Vitsyn[/b] (Project page on VK): [i]"It's better to replace those 4 game mode buttons with just 1. Or you could just keep adding them and end up filling the entire screen. [On the buttons at the top of the screen]".[/i]

We will come up with a solution for this in one of the next few updates. You will be able to choose multiplayer battles on the "globe" by marking the modes you are interested in and then starting an opponent search. Everything will be more consistent, more convenient, and more attractive.

[h1]Part 3: The Next Episode[/h1]

We'll probably tell you about the next update, but who knows? It will be a new blog season, after all ;)

notes.title: Development Blog #16
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/16d0ba83a228b1c3cebe86e4e718a00d754e9a01.png[/img]

[h1] Part 1. Finding a Path [/h1] 
Greetings, Officers!
Seasoned veterans of Blitzkrieg 3 might have already noticed better reactions from battle units under their command to their orders.

We agree that our pathfinding, or the algorithm for finding routes from point A to point B, was far from optimal for a very long time. Tanks exhibited poor navigational behavior in narrow passes and failed to interact with terrain obstacles properly. However, it was perfect for reenacting a big city driver in their natural habitat:

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/01.gif[/IMG]

The future of improving pathfinding was at first rather unclear. For quite a while, the team would just patch and polish what was already there – until it became clear that the gameplay demanded a completely new pathfinding algorithm.

Behind the new system is a huge body of intellectual and analytical effort from our programmer's time spent experimenting, testing theories, and researching new methods.

Our researchers trained our tank crews to race,
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/08.gif[/IMG]
turn into transformers,
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/03.gif[/IMG]
and politely avoid illegally parked drivers.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/04.gif[/IMG]

Funny bugs during this process were unavoidable. Take a look at what happens when you make a mistake when converting arcdegrees to radians:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/05.gif[/IMG]

After long iterations, we've succeeded in creating an efficient, fast, and well-optimised pathfinding system that allows the player to be fully submerged in commanding their army without having to deal with misunderstood orders.

Let's compare our old and new pathfinding systems with the help of this collection of GIFs.

[b]Old pathfinding[/b]: to avoid an obstacle, the Tank Destroyer stops, turns, and only then continues moving.
[IMG] http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/06.gif[/IMG]

[b]New pathfinding[/b]: the Tank Destroyer changes its direction while moving.
[IMG] http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/07.gif[/IMG]

Reporters from our battle front newspaper asked Artem Pavlenko, our chief officer, to share the details of the algorithms that shape the new pathfinding.

[b]Artem Pavlenko, Senior Programmer:[/b]:
[i] "The route for co-op pathfinding is built on a modified jump point search across layouts with a recursive clearance function that allows route calculation to account for the width of units.
Then the resulting high-level route is used with phantoms of the physical model in a swarming algorithm.
During movement, the route planner corrects the route based on the actual change of the position of the vehicle, which is modified indeterminately depending on the swarming algorithm phantoms."[/i] 

As you can see, writing a pathfinding algorithm really isn't that difficult!

[h1] Part 2. Our Week [/h1] 
And now, as usual, a few words from the development team about how the latest week went.

[b]Ivan Zvonarev, Balance Designer[/b]:
[i] "I dream of unit spreadsheets at night. For the past two weeks I've been adding new vehicles, new infantry, and new fortifications. I dug through a bunch of vehicle stats and reports to tune everything. I'm especially looking forward to the Wirbelwind and the KV-2. Then I'm planning to balance everything out. The game will have completely new unit models that require a bunch of work from scratch, and it's a great opportunity to fix some issues."[/i] 


[b]Manuel, Operations Manager[/b]:
[i] "The last days before releasing an update are the most nerve wrecking, because during playtests we discover new bugs that haven't been there before, and we have to make a choice between postponing the release or releasing an unpolished version on time. Devblogs have to be written, newsletters created, PR messages sent over to the press – and there are always unpredicted obstacles."[/i] 
[IMG] http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/16/38858Np.gif[/IMG]


[h1]Part 3. Coming up...[/h1]
Our next episode's topic will be the project's graphics. Time keeps ticking on, and the visual part of the game has been evolving. Our artists, animators, and graphic programmers will tell you about their work. Don't forget to check out the next dev blog!

See you on the battlefield, officers.

notes.title: Development Blog #15
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/DEVBLOG15_ENG.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Part 1: What's happening right now?[/h1]
Right now we're working on the update we promised (the one we talked about in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/604985283924292620]Development Blog #12[/url]). We'll describe some of the things we've done later in the post, where we usually put funny gifs about the atmosphere in our office :) 

Now, to our topic for today!

[h1]Polls are a delicate matter[/h1]
We started using polls actively about 7 months ago, once the required features had been introduced. Since then, we've conducted 17 polls. That means we've conducted an average of two and a half polls per month.

Perhaps we should've conducted more? Or perhaps less? Or maybe we should've changed the number of questions per poll? It's a difficult decision – we need to find out as much as possible, but it's also not a good idea to overburden players with a multitude of questions. So we've tried many poll formats during these 7 months. They included any number of questions between one and ten. We tried five-point scale and ten-point scale rating questions, comments sections, and multiple choice questions.
 
Anyway, if you think our polls should have more or fewer questions, please, don't hesitate to tell us! Also, we'll be very happy to hear any suggestions and ideas you have about improving the poll system in general.

The latest poll on Skirmish included only two points: one general question with an 10-point scale and a comments section. By the way, the results turned out to be pretty intriguing. 

When we analyse poll results, we usually distinguish among several categories of players. Here are the categories we used for the latest poll: 
[list][*]All players
[*]All 7-tier players
[*]New players (less than a month in the game)
[*]7-tier players with less than 3 months in the game
[*]Veterans (over a year in the game)[/list]

The results formed the following picture:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/POLL_ENG3.jpg[/IMG]

Looking at this, we can draw several conclusions:
[list][*]* Players with different playtime and progress amounts generally rate the game the same way.
[*]The average rating is "good".
[*]* The great bulk of replies are with a rating between 5 and 7, indicating that we could improve the game with a few updates to smooth it out. (We can't really do very much based on those who rated it from 1-3, because that would require remaking the game from scratch :)[/list]

So we've confirmed that we're moving in the right direction with the game's development, and we've prepared another poll that should help us understand what else could be changed to make our project even better and turn those 5-7 ratings into 8-10.

[b]The poll is already available in the game, so please let us know which aspect of the game we should concentrate on next.[/b]

[h1]Comments are even more delicate[/h1]
Communication via forums and social media is a whole different matter. Some of you (perhaps, many of you) have probably thought at one point, "Why didn't the developers listen to my suggestion, even though it got a few likes and several people even agreed with me?"
The thing is, not everybody on the Internet is inclined to write comments and participate in discussions. So, if we strictly followed forum suggestions, we'd be making the game only for the "loudest" people on the Internet. Besides, we regularly see vastly different ideas from the most active forum users. A good example was the suggestion to "make everything like it was in the first game". Later it turned out that "the first game" was different for everybody. Some people never logged out of GameSpy, while others beat the singleplayer campaign 5 times. Some played it only on a local network with a friend. All these people have very different impressions of the game's mechanics, rules, and pace. We're trying to create a game that simultaneously incorporates as many suggestions as possible, while also bringing in something new.

But that doesn't mean we ignore the comments altogether. We don't. We carefully collect them, analyse them, and look for things that can be implemented. At the same time, we don't always reply to every comment. And that's not just because we often have already done so "yesterday in another thread" but also because, if we did, our presence on the forums would be too strong. We'd look like a Big Brother hanging over forum users' heads.

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/BIGBRO.jpg[/IMG]

By the way, we're often asked about the aspects of the game that we haven't yet started working on at all. Things like clans or planned DLCs. Don't take it the wrong way when we dodge these questions or just remain silent. Or when we say that "we're going to think about your clan idea later". We mean it! We are going to think about it later, when we actually get to work on this feature :)

[h1]And now, as usual, a few words from the development team about their most recent week of work.[/h1]

[b]Sasha, Lead Technical Artist:[/b]
They (surprisingly!) aren't letting us show anything, but I was able to get some things into the blog.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/ARTISTS.jpg[/IMG]

[b]Sergey, lead community manager:[/b]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/VACATION.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Part 2: Player Suggestions[/h1]

Here's a suggestion from [b]Sclu[/b] (on the project's VK page): [i]"The game really needs a minimum reward of about 20-30% for losing in Skirmish. Imagine somebody plays a Skirmish battle. Then another one, then another one... they keep losing, they lose resources, they can't make any progress, and eventually they leave the game!"[/i]

You're absolutely right: this is a real problem. But we're going to solve it in a slightly different way, because we need to treat the cause, not the symptoms ;) 

The current situation is caused by the fact that players fighting in Skirmish are often at very different levels. We've made our matchmaking broader, and now a hardened veteran may end up facing a rather average player or vice versa. We did this to make it easier to find an opponent while the project is still under development. As we add separate ratings for different game modes and also take into account the player's level, this problem will go away on its own.

[b]Dante Psykowski[/b] (on the project's Facebook page) asked: [i]And why duration of skirmish is average 5 min !? 10 min max if i let enemy have 1 point ! Srsly who was working on this and not aware of too short timeframe.[/i]

The cause and the solution here are the same as with the previous question. Naturally, the fight won't take very long if you're a veteran player with over 200 hours in the game and you're facing a less-experienced opponent. 

[b]Stefan[/b] (on the project's Steam page) asked: [i]"Will the good old encyclopedia be returning in Blitzkrieg 3?" [/i]

We're planning to start working actively on the website soon. It already contains some basics, and we're going to develop them into a knowledge base. We may (possibly, but not definitely) add an in-game button to open the website knowledge base.

[h1]Part 3: The Next Episode[/h1]
In the next episode, we'll tell you about our work on pathfinding. We'll talk about our mistakes and how we fixed them. Don't miss it – it'll be fun :)

And that's not just because we often have already done so "yesterday in another thread" but also because, if we did, our presence on the forums would be too strong. We'd look like a Big Brother hanging over forum users' heads.

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/BIGBRO.jpg[/IMG]

By the way, we're often asked about the aspects of the game that we haven't yet started working on at all. Things like clans or planned DLCs. Don't take it the wrong way when we dodge these questions or just remain silent. Or when we say that "we're going to think about your clan idea later". We mean it! We are going to think about it later, when we actually get to work on this feature :)

[h1]And now, as usual, a few words from the development team about their most recent week of work.[/h1]

[b]Sasha, Lead Technical Artist:[/b]
They (surprisingly!) aren't letting us show anything, but I was able to get some things into the blog.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/ARTISTS.jpg[/IMG]

[b]Sergey, lead community manager:[/b]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/15/VACATION.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Part 2: Player Suggestions[/h1]

Here's a suggestion from [b]Sclu[/b] (on the project's VK page): [i]"The game really needs a minimum reward of about 20-30% for losing in Skirmish. Imagine somebody plays a Skirmish battle. Then another one, then another one... they keep losing, they lose resources, they can't make any progress, and eventually they leave the game!"[/i]

You're absolutely right: this is a real problem. But we're going to solve it in a slightly different way, because we need to treat the cause, not the symptoms ;) 

The current situation is caused by the fact that players fighting in Skirmish are often at very different levels. We've made our matchmaking broader, and now a hardened veteran may end up facing a rather average player or vice versa. We did this to make it easier to find an opponent while the project is still under development. As we add separate ratings for different game modes and also take into account the player's level, this problem will go away on its own.

[b]Dante Psykowski[/b] (on the project's Facebook page) asked: [i]And why duration of skirmish is average 5 min !? 10 min max if i let enemy have 1 point ! Srsly who was working on this and not aware of too short timeframe.[/i]

The cause and the solution here are the same as with the previous question. Naturally, the fight won't take very long if you're a veteran player with over 200 hours in the game and you're facing a less-experienced opponent. 

[b]Stefan[/b] (on the project's Steam page) asked: [i]"Will the good old encyclopedia be returning in Blitzkrieg 3?" [/i]

We're planning to start working actively on the website soon. It already contains some basics, and we're going to develop them into a knowledge base. We may (possibly, but not definitely) add an in-game button to open the website knowledge base.

[h1]Part 3: The Next Episode[/h1]
In the next episode, we'll tell you about our work on pathfinding. We'll talk about our mistakes and how we fixed them. Don't miss it – it'll be fun :)

notes.title: Development Blog #14
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20ENG.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Part 1: What's happening right now?[/h1]
Right now we are working on a big update [i](which we wrote about [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/598230758564383462]in the previous episode of the blog[/url])[/i], which will integrate all the elements of the game together. As the work hums along, we would like to share some of the unpublished facts about the historical campaign.

[h1]Special Operations Units[/h1]
You experience the war as a special forces commander, which means your role, although local, is crucial for the success of the whole battlefront. While the general forces are attacking (or defending), your units will turn the tide of the battle, implementing lighting war (Blitzkrieg) tactics.

Many battles will be fought side by side with the regular troops. Occasionally, some of their units will be put under your command due to the high priority of the operations entrusted to you.

Your mission as the special forces commander is to do whatever is possible and more to fulfil the orders that you receive, whatever they may be.

[h1]Germany[/h1]
The German campaign will be the first out of the three to become available and will be released no later than July 10. It will comprise the following key battles:
[list]
[*][b]Operation Fall Weiss [/b] (September 1, 1939) - [i]already available in the game![/i]
[*][b]Arras[/b] (May 21, 1940) - [i]already available in the game![/i]
[*][b]North Africa[/b] (March 31, 1941) - [i]already available in the game![/i]
[*][b]March on Daugavpils[/b] (June 1941) - [i]already available in the game![/i]
[*][b]Alamein[/b] (October-November 1942) - [i]the mission of your task force here is to attack a British supply base far behind enemy lines. Your goal is to distract the British and to strip their troops from the supplies they need for the offensive. You will be greatly outnumbered by the British, but you can rely on the support of Rommel’s retreating Panzer Army Africa.[/i]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20HISTORY%20PIC%201-5.jpg[/IMG]
[*][b]3rd Sevastopol Offensive[/b] (June 7 – July 4, 1942) - [i]supported by heavy vehicles, your task force has to break through to the shore of Severnaya Bay and ensure fire adjustment for the siege artillery on the mooring areas to prevent the Soviet command from transferring ammunition and reinforcements to Sevastopol.[/i]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20HISTORY%20PIC%202-2.jpg[/IMG]
[*][b]Ardennes Attack[/b] (December 1944) - [i]backed by heavy vehicles and jet aircraft, your squad must act behind the American lines, destroying HQs and supply bases.[/i]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20HISTORY%20PIC%203.jpg[/IMG]
[/list]

Of course, this list of missions is far from complete. There will be a whole series of additional battles, and we will try to tell you about them in one of the next episodes of the Development Blog. 
	
After our forced march to the update containing all these missions is complete, we still have a few issues to solve. The thing is, by the time the German campaign becomes available, not all the historical chronicles and cutscenes (plot-related videos rendered by the game engine) will be completed. We are planning to add them a little later.

Also, we have scheduled our time to adjust the difficulty and the duration of missions based on players’ reviews after the update [i](see more in Part 3 of this post).  [/i]

[h1]USSR[/h1]
We have already [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/598230758564383462]announced the list of the main Soviet missions[/url], so in this section some (stereotypically wintry) screenshots will speak for us. 

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20WINTER%201.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20WINTER%202.jpg[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20WINTER%203.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Allies[/h1]
For starters, we can confirm that we are working on missions set in the jungles of Southeast Asia. They are at a very early stage of development right now, so we will show them a little later.

[h1]“The Dora Mission”[/h1]
The Dora mission included in the Strategic and Deluxe editions will be added once the work on the global campaign is done.

All we can say for now is that it will tell the story of one of the conflicts near Leningrad.

[h1]And now, as usual, a few words from the development team about their most recent week of work.[/h1]
[b]Vadim, Lead Tester:[/b]	
After spending a very long time with non-stop testing.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20GIF%20VADIM.gif[/IMG]

[b]Sergey, lead community manager:[/b]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/14/DEVBLOG14%20MONKEY%20ENG.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Part 2: Player Suggestions[/h1]
We continue our tradition of [strike]ripping apart[/strike] reviewing players’ suggestions. Today we have a suggestion by [b]Sam[/b] , from the official forum: [i]he would like to be able to “get revenge.”[/i] 

This idea isn’t new, but it’s still very good. We will definitely go back to it and consider all the pros and cons once we deal with the social functions in the game. The chance that we will implement this in the game is rather high, but we will need to decide its priority in relation to the priority of other social features.

[h1]Part 3: The Next Episode [/h1]
To continue our glorious tradition of interacting with the game community, we have launched a poll for version 0.8.5. In the next episode, we will tell you how the opinion polls work – how the surveys are designed and conducted. 

In the meantime, to emphasise the importance of your vote, we'd like to remind you what we have done after previous polls: [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/1/490123938429890844/]we’ve improved the campaign missions[/url], [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/1/492378265880583553/]multiplayer[/url], and launched both [url=http://blitzkrieg.com/news/novye-direktivy]Assault PvP[/url] and [url=http://blitzkrieg.com/news/skirmish]Skirmish modes[/url].

So please take part in our polls! :)

notes.title: Update 0.8.5
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/UPDATES/085ENG.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]What's New?[/h1]
[list]
[*]We've added Skirmish! Your goal in this mode is to increase your score by capturing and holding control points. At the moment there is only one symmetrical map available, but we plan to add more. This map includes three control points and a number of fortified strategic points. Right now, it's very important for us to thoroughly test the playability of this game mode and the map. For example: for the final version of the map, we want to create the feeling that the German line of defense was recently here and that now a head-on battle for this line is taking place. You can learn more about Skirmish mode, and how it differs from Assault mode, in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/604985283924292620]developer diaries #12[/url].
[*]This new mode also presents previously unavailable fortifications, such as damaged tank pillboxes that cannot be assaulted, only destroyed. These can be a big help in defending captured points, but to use them, the player first needs to repair them.
[*]Skirmish includes 1v1, 2v2, and 3v3 battles. However, the matchmaking lobby is currently unavailable. We're planning to add it in the next update.
[*]Pathfinding has been completely reworked. Vehicles don't get "stuck" anymore and are better at reacting to orders and plotting courses. We mentioned this in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/598230758564383462]developer diaries #13[/url].
[*]We've added bump mapping for terrain textures.
[*]Unit attack priorities have been adjusted. 
[*]Once you have seen fortifications in the fog of war, you'll only see the status they had when you last saw them. You can also command a unit to attack them.
[*]The in-game options menu allows you to choose from several variants of how units are grouped in the reinforcements panel.
[*]Whenever you hover over any friendly, enemy, or neutral object during combat, you'll see a tooltip (a pop-up window) with information about the object's name, class, durability, and current HP.
[*]Fortifications are now more durable. They don't stop working after the first encounter, they can be recaptured several times without being destroyed, and they protect their positions throughout the whole game.
 [/list]

After a few days (on June 10), once we have a good idea of your impressions and an idea of the big picture, we'll arrange an in-game poll about this update. Don't forget to participate!

notes.title: Development Blog #13
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/13/DEVBLOG13_ENG.jpg[/IMG]

Dear friends, we're proud to present the second episode of our developer diaries. 

[h1]Part 1: What's happening right now?[/h1]

While one part of the team is working on improving Skirmish after our recent testing [i]([url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/604985283924292620]our previous blog article[/url] was about this mode, so check it out if you missed it!)[/i], the other part is preparing the next update. So let's talk about that!

The updates described below are planned for release before July 10, 2016. And don't forget that Skirmish will be available next week.

[h1]Multiplayer + Historical campaigns + New economics[/h1]

The main menu will be replaced with the globe you've already seen in the historical campaign in Blitzkrieg 3. After some serious revisions, it'll be a strategic screen where, like a real commander, you will be able to plan and perform operations: [list]
[*]Secondary historical battles (side missions);
[*]Main decisive battles from campaign stages;
[*]Multiplayer battles (Assault, Skirmish 1v1, 2v2, and 3v3).[/list]

To complete a stage of the war and move on to the next period, you must win a Decisive Battle. Secondary battle goals will be optional, and completing them will provide various rewards:[list]
[*]Units; 
[*]Experience;
[*]Commanders' trust[/list]

After wining a decisive battle, you can always go back and fight the earlier periods of the war (both in the single-player campaign and in multiplayer).  

But there's one small hitch. Completing a decisive battle to advance through the story requires us to complete all of the historical missions. Unfortunately, we haven't completed them all; by the time these features will be released, we'll only have the German campaign ready. So, for now it's going to work like this: if, for example, you're playing as the USSR, you'll control the Soviet army in all battles, but when you start a historical mission, your units will be temporarily replaced by German ones.

You might ask: why introduce this system now if not everything is ready yet? Well, because we can't test our new economics right before the game's release, so we need to do it now :)

By the way, we're going to introduce things smoothly, so there will be a "transition period." During this period, players will have a specific amount of resources for use purchasing an army, based on their rating and lots of other stats. Those who choose not to buy troops will get a standard set of units. So there's no point in buying a huge army just hoping it'll be transferred into the new economic system :) 

By the end, we'll have unique armies, and each individual unit will become more valuable, ultimately increasing the value of battles.

[h1]Player's Base[/h1]

The globe will be the first thing you see in the game (unless you've already chosen a faction when you first launched Blitzkrieg 3). Thus the player's base will also be located on the globe. 

You can't build and upgrade buildings on your part of the battlefield anymore, but you can raise defences using fortifications and units you have received for combat achievements.

The base itself is now a decoration which reflects the player's progress, both with the appearance of its buildings and by showing your best troops marching in front of your HQ.

Thus your combat achievements will be visible by looking at your base. 

[h1]And now, as usual, a few words from the development team about their most recent week of work.[/h1]

[b]Captain Morgan, Lead Programmer:[/b]
We've greatly improved pathfinding. You'll be able to see this for yourself after the next update. This doesn't mean we've stopped working on it, but we've achieved a whole new level of quality.

Before:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/13/DevBlog13_GIF_1.gif[/IMG]

After:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/13/DevBlog13_GIF_2.gif[/IMG]
We've now got a lot less standing around and passing through things now :)

[b]Vadim, Lead Tester:[/b]
For the QA team, this week was The Battle of the Bugs. Almost every bug was looked into, all in the framework of a friendly discussion... 
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/13/DevBlog13_GIF_3.gif[/IMG]
Then we followed that up with regular reminders so that our people would stay focused on fixing the bugs.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/13/DevBlog13_GIF_4.gif[/IMG]

[b]Sasha, Lead Technical Artist:[/b]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/13/DevBlog13_GIF_5.gif[/IMG]

[h1]Part 2: Player Suggestions[/h1]
We are still discussing player suggestions. Today on our table we've got a suggestion by [b]Lunar_Daemon[/b] from the official forum: [i]“I suggest increasing the time that effects like immobilisation and optics damage affect vehicles up to at least 1 minute.”[/i]

Let's imagine we've incorporated your idea. Which, by the way, is actually pretty great – but would only fit different basic game conditions. 

So, let's imagine that the player may lose an important part of their army for a minute (for example, a heavy tank which is essential for their assault). In that case, they'll most likely stop the assault and just wait around for a minute. 

So we'll need to introduce additional countermeasures (otherwise, the player will face an uncontrollable gameplay situation). Let's say we add something like a repair truck into the game. By doing this we're forcing the player to always have this truck with them. And forcing players to do things is bad. Especially on Blitzkrieg 3's scale. If this truck were just a little tool in a big army (i.e. if our gameplay was based on different principles), we could do that. But we've got to remind you that our armies aren't that big, and our system for acquiring new units increases the value of each new unit on the map. 

So we arrive at the basic principle of this game. It's meant to go at a moderate pace. In order to significantly increase the duration of a damage effect, we'd have to change lots of other things. We wouldn't be able to simply make it last longer. So this apparently doesn't fit into our current plans well; if we did make changes like this, developing the game might take forever. If you have any ideas about possible countermeasures we could introduce to balance out this kind of change, please share them with us in the commentary section :)

[h1]Part 3: The Next Episode [/h1]
To make the wait for the next episode (which will be centered around historical campaigns) a little more interesting, here's a list of battles that Soviet troops will be fighting in Blitzkrieg 3: Luga, Rzhev, Sevastopol, Stalingrad, Kursk, Warsaw, Berlin. 

What do you think: which battles will we introduce for the USA and Germany?

[*]Secondary historical battles (side missions);
[*]Main decisive battles from campaign stages;
[*]Multiplayer battles (Assault, Skirmish 1v1, 2v2, and 3v3).[/list]

[*]Units; 
[*]Experience;
[*]Commanders' trust[/list]

After wining a decisive battle, you can always go back and fight the earlier periods of the war (both in the single-player campaign and in multiplayer).

Unfortunately, we haven't completed them all; by the time these features will be released, we'll only have the German campaign ready. During this period, players will have a specific amount of resources for use purchasing an army, based on their rating and lots of other stats. Those who choose not to buy troops will get a standard set of units. So there's no point in buying a huge army just hoping it'll be transferred into the new economic system :) 

By the end, we'll have unique armies, and each individual unit will become more valuable, ultimately increasing the value of battles.

The globe will be the first thing you see in the game (unless you've already chosen a faction when you first launched Blitzkrieg 3). Thus the player's base will also be located on the globe. 

You can't build and upgrade buildings on your part of the battlefield anymore, but you can raise defences using fortifications and units you have received for combat achievements.

notes.title: Development Blog #12
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/DEVBLOG_12_EN.jpg[/IMG]

Friends, we’re proud to present a new season of our regular Development Blog, which is updated every Friday. Here you can learn about our day-to-day work and upcoming changes to the game. During the break we thought of plenty of interesting topics, so let’s dive right in.

[h1]Part 1: “What’s happening right now?”[/h1]

Following recent commentary and the results of the poll on update 0.8 ([i]which you can check out [url=http://blitzkrieg.com/news/update0801]here[/url] and [url=http://blitzkrieg.com/news/hotfixes0802]here[/url][/i]), we turned our attention towards full-blown internal testing of Skirmish mode.

This long-awaited game mode will be available on public servers beginning on the 10th of June. By that time, we will have prepared a basic version with fully-functional gameplay, but it’ll still be somewhat unpolished (this will be fixed in future updates). For example, the matchmaking system will select random opponents and allies, but you’ll soon be able to assemble a team of your friends.

[b]How Skirmish is different from Assault:[/b]
[list][*]It includes 2v2 and 3v3 modes and thus involves more teamwork.
[*]The map is completely symmetrical.
[*]Players don’t have a predefined line of defence with fortifications and don’t have bases.
[*]The map has additional points of interest that give a tactical advantage or have fortifications.
[*]The rate of your Reinforcement Point generation depends not on your number of captured control points but rather on the size of your army (the larger your army, the slower your points generate).
[*]The player’s goal is to obtain a certain number of points by controlling the control points.[/list]

The map layout is typical for this kind of game mode: there’s a “home” control point next to the deployment area, and there’s a control point in the centre which is set at an equal distance from both teams.  

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_SKIRMISH_5.png[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_SKIRMISH_4.png[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_SKIRMISH_3.png[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_SKIRMISH_2.png[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_SKIRMISH_1.png[/IMG]

The most obvious tactic is to capture the closest point and then move towards the centre of the map. However, the best way to secure victory is to experiment with various tactical approaches: capturing points in a different order, maneuvering, and supporting. This is where the points of interest come in, since they allow players to utilise unconventional tactics. The greater the number of players, the more opportunities they’ll have to try out complex approaches.

And now, as usual, [h1]a few words from the development team about their most recent week.[/h1]

[b]Vadim, Lead Tester:[/b]
Three patches over the last three weeks. We had a lot of work to do, so we never stopped bothering the programmers, even during lunch breaks...
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_gif1.gif[/IMG]
In general, this is how we feel now:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_gif2.gif[/IMG]

[b]Sasha, Lead Technical Artist:[/b]
There’s been an addition to our friendly, close-knit team!  
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_gif3.gif[/IMG]
One of our interesting and not-too-secret developments is that we’ve made great progress increasing the quality of terrain. The soil will soon be much cooler and more volumetric ;)

[b]Jean, Lead Designer:[/b]
Recently, while working on a winter-themed map, we encountered a funny bug that turned snow into cake icing.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_pic1.png[/IMG]

[b]Captain Morgan, Lead Programmer:[/b]
Skirmish, Skirmish, more Skirmish...
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/12/Dev12_gif4.gif[/IMG]

[h1]Part 2: “Player suggestions”[/h1]
This season, we’re presenting this new column. We’ll be taking a couple of player suggestions to [strike]rip them apart[/strike] discuss them :) 

In this first post we’ll discuss a suggestion by [b]Knightbruder[/b] posted on the official forum: [i]“I suggest giving the sniper the ability to fire while camouflaged without losing the camouflage bonus.”[/i]

This would cause the sniper to become a real Predator, an uber-effective AI-destroyer and a thorn in enemy players’ sides. 
 
His low fire rate and low fire density would make it impossible to identify the source of the shot, even indirectly, thus turning the game into an excruciating fight against a ghost. Earlier, some players used to wear out their opponents at the forest edge with just one sniper. With a change like this, we would turn the whole map into “the forest.” 
 
Besides, pixel-hunting in 2016 is just not cool. When the player can’t see or understand what’s happening and why, that’s bad. For instance, imagine that you had to follow a recon aircraft with your camera to record the location of some fortifications. With a “Predator sniper,” you’d have to watch each and every soldier at all times, leaving you unable to take the measures necessary to complete your strategic objective :)

[h1]Part 3: “The Next Episode”[/h1]
To make the wait for the next Episode a little more interesting, here are a few highlights from the next blog post:
[list][*]The historical campaigns will reflect the player’s progress. By the way, there will be 3 of these (playing as USSR, as Germany, and as the USA), and each of them will gradually bring the player through the war. The first campaign will be released in the early summer of 2016.
[*]You’ll need to take troops from your own army into the historical campaigns. Your people will go through the whole war alongside of you, carrying their experience from 1939 to 1945 (vehicle crews will be able to be switched to newer vehicles whenever you’re able and willing to do so).
[*]The new economy will make it impossible to just buy everything (for example, you won’t be able to buy tanks – you’ll be rewarded with them by Command for successfully completing operational objectives). Your most valuable asset will be your army.
[/list]

notes.title: Hotfix
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/0802bUSA.jpg[/IMG]

A small update has been deployed, which has fixed an issue with the Assault mode winning conditions. In some cases, the winner was wrongly designated, receiving ressources and rating without meeting the winning criteria.

[b]The winning conditions for both sides are now as follows:[/b][list]
[*]Destroy opponents Headquarters
[*]Destroy opponents Communication Centre and all units
[*]Opponent leaves the game
[/list]
[b]How is it determined, if a victory is minor or major (attacker)?[/b][list]
[*]Triumph - the attacker wins (according to the above mentioned conditions), managing to capture at least one control point.
[*]Victory - the attacker wins without capturing any control points
[*]Defeat - the attacker loses, with at least one control point captured
[*]Crushing Defeat- the attacker loses without capturing any control points at all.
[/list]
For the defending player, the victory conditions are a mirror reflection of the above-mentioned list.

notes.title: Patch 0.8.0.1
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/STEAM08_hotfixes_EN.jpg[/IMG]

After reviewing your feedback, we have decided to increase the significance of pre-planned defense in relation to direct combat defense. To achieve this, we have increased the limit of the troops and fortifications for the defender, and at the same time reduced the impact of reinforcement points flow from CP.

[B]Set the following limits:[/B]
[LIST]
[*]Assaulter set limit: 250/300/400/525/650/775/900
[*]Defender set limit: 150/225/300/350/400/450/500
[*]Fortifications limit: 130/130/190/250/305/380/475
[*]Maximum limit of  the army in the battle: 450/525/650/775/900/1050/1200
[/LIST]

[B]Parameters of the reinforcement points were modified:[/B]
[LIST]
[*]The basic generation was reduced to 3 points per 5 seconds.
[*]Generation for the owning a CP (control points) was reduced to 1,5/2,25/3 for 1/2/3 CP.
[*]A multiplier was moved to after ⅙ of standard combat timer, gradually increasing the reinforcement point generation until a maximum at ½ of the combat session timer
[*]The maximum of this multiplier was increased to 3.5.
[/LIST]

[B]Other balancing changes:[/B]
[LIST]
[*]The starting values of the delay on the support for defend side were increased:
Bomber and attack aircraft:  180/210/240s for levels 1/2/3.
Howitzer: 180s.
[*]Snipers’ survivability was reduced to 33% of original value..
[*]MRLS vehicles now do increased damage by 50%.
[*]Durability of buildings was increased by 35%.
[*]Shrapnel damage on garrisoned infantry in buildings was increased by 200%.
[/LIST]

notes.title: Update 0.8
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/08steamEN.jpg[/IMG]

In anticipation of the celebration of the end of the War in the European Theatre, we would like to invite you, commanders, to try this big new update full of exciting changes. 

[h1]What’s new?[/h1]
[list]
[*]Three new missions for the German campaign: North Africa, Daugavpils Rush, and Arras.
[*]Completely redesigned Assault mode:
1)	The player’s main objective (victory condition) is to destroy the enemy’s headquarters, instead of the earlier requirement to capture the Control Points within a particular period of time;
2)	Control Points are now points of interest for the player, not the final objective. Their role is secondary: they increase Reinforcement Point generation;
3)	A new reinforcement summoning system has been introduced: the player uses Reinforcement Points to request troops from the base that haven’t been used as advance forces (all the troops available at the base are available in battle).
4)	Reinforcement Points are continually earned during the battle, as well as when a Control Point is successfully captured. The amount of points credited depends on the number of Control Points under the player’s control: each subsequent CP captured will grant fewer points. For instance, when you capture your first control point (or re-capture it after losing all of your control points), you score more points for it than for the last control point.
5)	Opponents have varying cooldown (recharge time) and point limits. The attacker has many more troops at the beginning of the battle, but the defender has three Control Points and a quicker Reinforcement Point generation rate. 
6)	This approach allows for a “see-saw” system, making it easy to get back into the battle. Example: the attacker has thrown all his troops into the battle and almost made it to the HQ. Meanwhile the defender managed to save up enough points and summoned troops that effectively resisted the attacking force. Once the attacker has been driven back to his starting position, he can summon forces optimally suited to fight the defender’s current forces. Thus players will be able to steal the initiative from each other. 
7)	The attacker now has a reinforcement point for his attack, a base of sorts. The defender’s base has also been redesigned. Destroying the enemy’s HQ now automatically scores a victory, while destroying their Communication Centre deprives them of reinforcements and supports.
[*]The central panel has been redesigned for battle. A reinforcement panel has been added, and the support panel has been redesigned. However, the interface is still not informative enough, and a number of our solutions are temporary. We are working hard on it and will soon improve the situation. 
[*]New thematic loading screens have been added.
[*]The launcher has been removed for all Steam players. News and maintenance announcements are now shown in the main menu, and updating is conducted via Steam servers.
[*]Numerous balance adjustments: unit speed, support cooldown time, ranged effects. We are still working on this and will continue doing so far into the future. So we’d greatly value your comments about the balance of our redesigned Assault mode.
[*]Players can place more infantry squads in some houses than in others, depending on their size.
[*]New support added: Fighter. Smoke Screen and Paratroopers supports have been reworked. Paratroopers now land from aircraft which can be shot down.
[*]The defending AI now uses supports and reacts to the player’s actions more aggressively and actively. But we are still working on this, and significant improvements will be ready by May or June.
[*]Steam authorisation has been significantly sped up; the Leaderboard now loads much more quickly.
[/list]

[h1]Fixed Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*]Improved game stability (frequent crashes were reported after the January 27th patch).
[*]Several squads can now be treated at the same time on the first mission of the Single Player campaign (Poland).
[*]The crashes during the town capture in the first mission of the Single Player campaign (Poland) have been fixed.
[*]An issue causing incomplete update installation when there is insufficient hard disk space (freezing during the game logo) has been fixed.
[*]Flags used during battle have been replaced with correct ones (the attacker’s flags were previously shown on the defender’s Control Points).
[*]Paratroopers no longer “jump” on the roofs of buildings while walking.
[*]The incorrect behaviour of the patrolmen in the first mission of the Single Player campaign (Poland) has been fixed: when troops were trying to circle around a patrol, and at the start of battle, the patrolmen continued walking along their routes as if nothing had happened.
[*]We’ve fixed an incorrect behaviour of infantry during an abrupt change in movement direction: an infantry squad, when ordered to run in the opposite direction, used to first turn towards where ordered but then resume moving in its initial direction.
[/list]

[h1]Known problems to be fixed later:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Attack Aircraft attacks base buildings instead of units
[*]Incorrect location of icons on the minimap
[*]Reinforcements available to call after the battle is over
[*]Upgrading a fortification cancels the selection
[*]When leaving trenches, infantry doesn’t follow orders
[*]Severe game freezing when capturing a building with obstructions using several infantry squads
[*]No visual effects for AT landmine explosions
[*]Incorrect animation of snipers when shooting
[*]Units stand above a trench while sitting in it
[*]Cutscenes in the Daugavpils mission may work incorrectly (lag) on some PC configurations 
[*]Objects on the minimap may be displayed incorrectly (with their positions shifted)
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.7.2
notes.content:
[IMG]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/312244513767631974/00B03FB73BD4DD5289328AE296930AE22FE3AD7E/[/IMG]

Good afternoon, commander!

By popular demand of the commissioned officers of the battlefronts and armies, the Blitzkrieg 3 Experimental Establishment has thoroughly inspected the current combat system to implement a higher level of realism.
[list]
[*]In earlier versions of the game, battles were not always like real life. Soldiers could be injured by a dozen rifle bullets and still be alive. Now most combat units are destroyed with a few hits, but the chances a unit will miss have been increased to compensate. 
[*]New random weather effects have been added to the Multiplayer Campaign: rain and fog. Each of these significantly affects combat tactics.
[*]Moving targets are harder to hit, but firing while moving is harder, too.
[*]Now all infantry units are capable of capturing buildings, but Assault Infantry remain the most effective.
[*]Mines have become invisible. Regular Infantry can use their Clear Minefield ability without restraints.
[*]Bunkers can be stormed and re-captured.
[*]Unit visibility ranges have been changed. To deliver fire effectively across long distances, Tanks and Tank destroyers need infantry support.
[*]Tactical support actions have been completely rebalanced, with all unrealistic types being removed.
[*]Some types of Tank Destroyers now have an indirect fire option, just like their real-world counterparts.
[*]The player now must press any key to start the battle once the map/mission is completely loaded.
[*]Improved leaderboards UI.
[*]Single-player missions have been reworked to adjust to the new balance.
[/list]
Nival Headquarters hopes that battlefront and army commanders will like these changes and calls for detailed feedback in the comments section.
