notes.title: Skirmish Mode details revealed
notes.content:
[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=9681&d=1456156073[/IMG]

Friends, as you know, we’ve been working on some new game modes. Today, we are going to talk about skirmishes. 

[h1]Keynotes:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Players get Victory Points for holding key points (KPs). If a player has taken over all the KPs and controls the map completely, they gain points at a significantly faster rate. This way, an obviously more powerful opponent will win faster instead of “torturing” their weaker opponent in a prolonged fight. 
[*]If you completely destroy the enemy army, the game will end immediately – even if your enemy could have called for reinforcements.
[*]During the course of the game, players receive Reinforcement Points, which they can spend to summon reinforcements such as additional Units and fire support to the deployment zones. 
[*]The bigger the army and the more Reinforcement Points a player has, the fewer Reinforcement Points they receive. This correlation is not linear but happens in 2 to 4 stages: e.g. 300, 600, and 900 Reinforcement Points. This mechanic allows a player who has lost a significant part of their army to recuperate fairly quickly, call for several Units at once, and get back to the battlefield.
[*]Using support in skirmish mode will be different from all of the other modes. Instead of the Support Point Bar, the player will have Charges. A player gets Support Charges with Reinforcement Points. The Charges then appear on the Support Panel. Once used, a Charge disappears. If that was the last Charge, then the support disappears, and the player will have to re-buy it with Reinforcement Points. 
[*]Each side (or each player) has a small “base” in the deployment zone. The buildings inside let the player use support and summon reinforcements. We may add other features later on (e.g. equipment repairs, Ability Charge refills, etc.). Base buildings can be destroyed in order to cut the player off from their fire support and reinforcements. So players must keep in mind the need to protect their starting point, as well as captured key points.
[*]Neutral key points are considered captured once they are occupied by one and only one army. To capture an enemy key point, you must destroy all enemy units within it and then defend it during any assault. You won’t be able to hold all the key points at once, since that would require splitting your army. We figure that enemies will try to attack weakened KPs, making their own KPs vulnerable, and so on.
[*]There are various point of interest on each skirmish map, such as key points, player deployment zones, and neutral fortifications. These points of interest serve different gameplay purposes: some of them are a direct way to victory, while others are a more roundabout way. They make players split their attention and armies. They make them choose which points need troops and which are insignificant. In the future we are planning on a feature that will allow us to add special points of interest according to the map type: a tank factory, a radio facility for powering up your support, a hospital for restoring your squad’s health, and so on. We are also planning to add diverse landscaping including hills, rocks, forests, and settlements, affecting your tactical choices and battle gameplay.
[/list]

So, what do you think of all this? What else would you like to know about skirmishes?

notes.title: Update 0.7.1
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/STEAM071EN.jpg[/IMG]

We have fully focused our work on making global improvements and testing new game modes. In the meantime, we have prepared a number of fixes for the current update:
[list]
[*]First of all, we have fixed and improved the first mission of Invasion of Poland, the German campaign. 
[*]Bomber support has been added to the Multiplayer support pool. When called in, bombers deal significant area damage.
[*]The Saboteur support has been modified. The unit now plants a “package” behind enemy lines which stuns enemies with an explosion instead of distracting them. 
[*]You can now place infantry units in any fortification except Machine Gun Bunkers, after destroying the current garrison. This means that if you attack a fortification with light caliber guns and kill all the units inside, your troops can capture the guns.
[*]The Fortification Capture support has been removed.
[*]There is now a button to force all the infantry controlled by the player to go prone. From now on, units go prone and crawl only when the respective command is given. AI controlled units go prone using the same triggers as before.
[*]The Little Italy map has been reworked; all new players will now have the new version. Map edges have been improved, and another deployment area has been added.
[*]Defense Testing Battle Reports have been modified, and misleading information has been removed. Defense Testing Battles are no longer included in the reports.
[*]The start mission button in historical campaign has been modified.
[*]Backwards movement speed now runs at 70% of normal speed.
[/list]

[h1]Patch 0.7.0 Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Added two Historical Campaign missions: Invasion of Poland and Siege of Sevastopol.
[*]Added a new mission selection screen for the Historical Campaign. Operations are unlocked chronologically as you progress through the game. When an operation is selected, the status of the fronts and brief information about the operation are displayed.

[*]Tooltips have also been added to missions to inform you of new objectives.
[*]The Mac OS version of the game has been launched. System requirements will be announced soon, but we already know that the minimum requirements are almost exactly the same as those for Windows.
[*]The economy has been tweaked to reduce the time players spend on the lowest tiers. 
[*]Added a Contacts tab to chat. Now you can right-click on a player’s nickname to add them to Contacts and easily track their status (Online/Offline).

notes.title: Update 0.6.10
notes.content:
[h1]What's New[/h1]

[b]1)[/b]Since some players who didn't want to lose their defence rating switched to twinks when they were absent, we have added a 48-hour cooldown between base changes. After moving to a different base, players will only be able to move again after two days.

[b]2)[/b]To encourage better use of MLRS, we have added charges limiting their use per session. There are now only 5 salvos for both attack and defence, which should be enough to receive the necessary fire support without using scorched earth tactics.

[b]3)[/b]The starting time has been increased to 70-75% of the total time pool. Also, you will now get +10%, +15%, or +25% for a captured control point (depending on how many points there are on the map).

[b]4)[/b]Aircraft have been rebalanced once again. Their support point cost has been reduced. Damage dealt to vehicles by assault infantry has been increased.

[b]5)[/b]Many types of support are now more effective:
[list]
[*]Smoke Screen's duration has been increased by 50%
[*]Number of shells have been increased for Howitzer Salvo and Howitzer Fire
[*]Howitzer support cooldown has been increased to 1 second
[*]The cost to Capture Fortification has been reduced to 3 (2 if the Fortification is a Commander's)
[*]The cost of engineer support has been reduced to 1 (but range has been increased by 30%, if the support belongs to a Commander)
[/list]

[b]6)[/b]The cost of howitzers (fortifications) in support points has been increased from 62 to 69.


[b]7)[/b]The number of available obstructions has been reduced by a third.

[b]8)[/b]Combat controls have been updated:
[list]
[*]Right-clicking a unit's icon in the central panel centres the camera on the unit, instead of highlighting all identical units as before. You can still highlight all identical units by right-clicking one of them on the map or by holding Ctrl and left-clicking the unit.
[*]Pressing Shift + a number adds highlighted units to the group assigned to that number. If there is no group assigned to this number, the shortcut works the same as Ctrl+Number.
[/list]

[b]9)[/b]All Generals have been renamed Commanders, which is a more accurate word for the tasks they perform. This does not include texts where "general" is used to describe the Commander's rank.

notes.title: Update 0.6.10
notes.content:
[h1]What's New[/h1]

[b]1)[/b]Since some players who didn't want to lose their defence rating switched to twinks when they were absent, we have added a 48-hour cooldown between base changes. After moving to a different base, players will only be able to move again after two days.

[b]2)[/b]To encourage better use of MLRS, we have added charges limiting their use per session. There are now only 5 salvos for both attack and defence, which should be enough to receive the necessary fire support without using scorched earth tactics.

[b]3)[/b]The starting time has been increased to 70-75% of the total time pool. Also, you will now get +10%, +15%, or +25% for a captured control point (depending on how many points there are on the map).

[b]4)[/b]Aircraft have been rebalanced once again. Their support point cost has been reduced. Damage dealt to vehicles by assault infantry has been increased.

[b]5)[/b]Many types of support are now more effective:
[list]
[*]Smoke Screen's duration has been increased by 50%
[*]Number of shells have been increased for Howitzer Salvo and Howitzer Fire
[*]Howitzer support cooldown has been increased to 1 second
[*]The cost to Capture Fortification has been reduced to 3 (2 if the Fortification is a Commander's)
[*]The cost of engineer support has been reduced to 1 (but range has been increased by 30%, if the support belongs to a Commander)
[/list]

[b]6)[/b]The cost of howitzers (fortifications) in support points has been increased from 62 to 69.


[b]7)[/b]The number of available obstructions has been reduced by a third.

[b]8)[/b]Combat controls have been updated:
[list]
[*]Right-clicking a unit's icon in the central panel centres the camera on the unit, instead of highlighting all identical units as before. You can still highlight all identical units by right-clicking one of them on the map or by holding Ctrl and left-clicking the unit.
[*]Pressing Shift + a number adds highlighted units to the group assigned to that number. If there is no group assigned to this number, the shortcut works the same as Ctrl+Number.
[/list]

[b]9)[/b]All Generals have been renamed Commanders, which is a more accurate word for the tasks they perform. This does not include texts where "general" is used to describe the Commander's rank.

notes.title: DevBlog 11
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/dev11.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]The Player Surveys[/h1]
The recent survey of our players’ opinions showed a pressing need for more time and resources to be spent on polishing a number of different things.

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/Dev11_1.gif[/IMG]

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791434118091/announcements/detail/75792763548453844]In Episode 8 of the Development Blog[/url] we discussed how our decision to improve the single-player campaign had been made based on the results of an earlier survey. Now, it seems that it’s the turn of the multiplayer! 

The average score that multiplayer received in its current form is 3.3 out of 5, which shows an evident need to give it some more attention. You’ll start to see some of the changes very soon (we’ll discuss how soon in the final part of this entry), but the vast majority of the improvements we need to make will be introduced gradually, as we move closer to the final release date.

[h1]The Release Date[/h1]
Speaking of which, with the scope of the work we’re talking about here, we have very little time left and unfortunately, it simply won’t be enough to get everything in that you’ve been asking us for before we release. You know, bug-hunting is a hard job!

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/Dev11_2.gif[/IMG]

As such, we’ve decided to move the release date to the first quarter of 2016. This will allow us to get Blitzkrieg 3’s quality up to the desired level.

[h1]The Next Update[/h1] 
Most of the team is still focused on tweaking the single-player campaign (you’ll be able to assess the first results of their work in Version 0.7.0), but next week we’ll be bringing you the smaller Update 0.6.10. This will implement some of the most popular recent community requests, including:
[list]
[*]Limiting MLRS ammo to try and improve the situation for defenceless AI when defending a base,
[*]Rebalancing to accommodate the most recent changes (in particular, one of the most popular requests – more time at the beginning of battles),
[*]A cooldown period when moving to a different base (to prevent players dominating the leaderboards by switching to a different base before leaving the game, thus making their dethronement impossible)
[/list]

Finally, what do you want to see in the game as soon as possible? Let us know in the comments! :)

notes.title: Update 0.6.9
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2015/069miniweb.jpg[/IMG]
•	The Blitzkrieg 3 game engine has been transferred to the new version of Unity (Unity 5). This will help us speed up the development process and continue to improve the game. Because of the update, all game content has undergone changes, and this has resulted in a large update.
•	Players can now buy any number of any fortifications and place them at their discretion, limited only by their fortifications Supply Points (dependant on map and player tier).
•	The upgrade system has been redesigned. We have also added the MLRS upgrade, the third upgrade option, and the fifth Gear for all units.
•	The gear system has new stats. For example, the stealth upgrade that decreases the detection range of a unit in forests and tall grass.
•	A new default unit ability, Hold Fire, has been added to the game. If selected, units won’t attack until they are spotted. Without Hold Fire mode, units will attack enemies in range irrespective of their stealth status.
•	Session timer mechanics and the number of Support Points have changed. Now, when a battle begins players get less time and Support Points, but gain more time and Support Points for capturing Control Points.
•	Anti-aircraft guns are now able to attack infantry and vehicles. Aircraft remain high-priority targets.
•	Search limits will now be expanded in matchmaking if no players are found in the specified range of base power/rank.
•	The mechanics of machine gun fire have changed. Now, machine gunners don’t fire all of their bullets in a burst at one infantryman target, but instead spray the area with a certain amount of scatter. Also, when machine guns fire, a suppression effect is applied to the target, forcing enemies to get down and reducing some of their combat stats.
•	The ability to fire at specifically-designated areas has been added for machine gun squads. All infantry in the target area will take damage and have the suppression effect applied to them.
•	All aircraft have been rebalanced to make them stronger.
•	Units, fortifications, and limits have been rebalanced in the first few tiers. Battles are now slower and units harder to kill.
•	The economy in the first few tiers has been recalculated.

===

notes.title: DevBlog 10
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2015/devblog10miniweb.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Competition: What Do Soldiers Say?[/h1]
We all love the voice work in the first and second Blitzkrieg games. But the Blitzkrieg 3 team isn’t resting on its laurels, and we’re planning to significantly diversify both our voiceover phrases and the situations that trigger them.

To that end, we’d like to announce the Competition for Player-Written Unit Dialogue!

To enter, simply leave your ideas for new unit lines in the comments section of the Developer Diaries No. 10 news item on Steam, on the Blitzkrieg 3 website, on the game’s official forum, or anywhere you find it in your social networks. All ideas must contain: the name of the unit, its faction, the line itself, and the trigger (situation)that will cause the line to be played. For example:

1) Unit: Infantry Squad, USA
2) Line: “Take that!”
3) Trigger: An enemy unit is destroyed by the squad

We’ll be monitoring for and considering your ideas until November the 16. The best lines will be recorded by professional actors and added to the game!

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog10_1.gif[/IMG]

[h1]Unity 5.0[/h1]
Now then, you can expect the next patch to be quite large. Thanks to the intense work of our programmers, we’ve finally updated our Unity engine from version 4.6 to 5.0. This has reshaped the course of the entire project, and allows us to implement more advanced solutions when developing new features. How do we feel about this Unity update? Take a look at this:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog10_2.gif[/IMG]

So, we’ve done it! ːsteamhappyː

Also on the technical front, we’ve begun finalising the Mac version, in order to make it available to players as soon as possible.

[h1]Game Balance[/h1]
Finally, we’d like to tell you about some new balance adjustments, since we receive a lot of questions and comments on the balancing which are very often contradictory. For example, one player will say anti-tank infantry are too strong, and another that they’re too weak. So how do we balance the numbers in cases like that?

It’s all quite simple. ːsteamhappyː
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog10_3.gif[/IMG]
We have a statistics system that accumulates data on various in-game processes, such as which units are being used and which Generals are commanding them, as well as various skills, level numbers and support types. All that information is then checked against its win ratio, so we can see quite clearly when something is under- or over-performing. A good example is General Konev – previously, he was too far ahead of the other Generals, winning a good 90% of his battles. So we dialled him back a bit, and now he’s an effective commander, but not a dominant one.

===

notes.title: DevBlog 9
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2015/Devblog9Miniweb.jpg[/IMG]

Last time, we looked at the general future of the single-player campaign, so now we’d like to give you some information on upcoming multiplayer innovations. The difference is that the things we’re discussing today don’t cover the overall plan for multiplayer, but just the upcoming plans. As a matter of fact, we’re working on them right now. ːsteamhappyː

[h1]Difficult Choice [/h1]
Developers of strategic games always have to think about how to increase variability in their gameplay. Making a deep game with a great number of possible situations can be achieved in different ways. For example, we already have Generals, that allow the player to try combining different units and support types, and now we’re preparing another important feature for the forthcoming update. 
The well-known upgrade system (Gears) will be logically enhanced to allow you to create non-diversified unit builds (using Gears for upgrading fortification systems will be added a bit later). For example, you’ll be able to turn your infantry into light, agile, hidden squads, or put all your resources into increasing their firepower. 
Combinations of different units strengthened by a range of special skills and supported by the Generals’ own special skills will allow you to create unique armies, tuned for your favourite combat styles.
By the way, units that currently don’t have any upgrades (for example, MLRS) will be getting them eventually too. 

[h1]Defending the Sky and the Land[/h1]
As promised, stationary and self-propelled AA guns will destroy not only enemy aircraft but ground forces as well. This means not only the implementation of an additional fire mode, but also AA guns’ own development line in the Gears system.

[h1]Mine Camouflage[/h1]
Something else we promised earlier that is now being implemented, is that you can only see mines when you are close to them. A bit later on, we’ll be making so that Generals will be able to use special mine camouflage to make them practically invisible – attacking players will only find these little ‘surprises’ when they’re almost right on top  of them.

[h1]Time and Support Depend on Battlefield Success[/h1]
The combat timer and Support Points will be bound to Control Points. In order to get additional Support Points, you will have to capture at least one CP. In this way, battles for each piece of land will become more fierce, encounters will depend more on unit actions, and you will have to use your Support Points even more wisely.

[h1]Flexible Matchmaking[/h1]
The matchmaking system goes through different stages, activated incrementally when a search is made. At first, your opponent is selected based on technical development (base building levels). If no suitable opponent is found, the next stage includes a wider range of similar rankings. Now, the matchmaking system has been slightly tweaked to make it more flexible, meaning searches for opponents should be more effective.

[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
Machine gunners will deal area damage, blanketing enemies with suppressive fire. 
A new type of damage (fragmentation damage) and protection from it, is also upcoming.
Fortifications now have a separate total supply limit, to be used at your discretion. For example, you can use all your stock on howitzers, or spend it all on bunkers.

notes.title: DevBlog 8
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2015/bb30c.jpg[/IMG]

Dear Soldiers,
Based on the results of our previous surveys, the average grade awarded to our single-player campaign is 3.3 out of 5. This is a clear message to us that we should pay more attention to this part of the project.

As such, we’ve decided to raise the bar even higher for the historical campaign system (the campaign map, mission sequencing, support etc). This new episode of the Diaries comes to you directly from Andrey, our Lead Level Designer, and is fully dedicated to what we’re doing to make the single-player campaign a proper five-star General! 

[h1]Fighting on Three Fronts[/h1]
We can single out three main strategic areas of work in preparing for the full release of the single-player campaign:
[list]
[*]Upgrading available missions,
[*]Developing the campaign system (UI elements, briefings, global map, historical chronicles),
[*]Developing new missions.
[/list]
So, first of all, let’s take a look at:

[h1]Quality Standards[/h1]
As you’ve probably already noticed, we’ve hidden nearly all of the previously available missions in order to do further work on them. Our strategy in doing so is based on the results of internal studio play tests, analysis of player comments, and our periodic surveys.

The main issue we’re focusing on is ensuring proper UI quality. All events, the minimap and UI signals, pop-up messages and voice instructions will be synchronized, to help the player control the situation rather than make them feel panicked. 

We’re also doing lots of bug fixes here. For example, in Operation Niwi, it can happen that saboteurs manage to lay mines on the bunker only every other time. Sometimes, they just gather around it for a friendly chat while waiting for your next orders. Soldiers must strictly obey their commander’s orders, you know!

We might make a few changes to the player’s objectives as well.

[h1]Historical Immersion[/h1]
Those of you who’ve had a chance to play the previous Blitzkriegs might remember the briefings and the strategic maps, which really helped immerse you in the historical background of the games. In keeping with this fine tradition, we’re preparing something similarly interesting here, too. You’ll be able to embrace the whole theatre of operations with your eyes, watch fragments of real films made at the time, and read interesting descriptions of concomitant events. 

We’ll be able to properly evaluate the results of the campaign system’s implementation in the update after the next update. The plan is to give you access to this content in Version 0.7.0, along with a new map, Sevastopol.

[h1]The Battles to Come [/h1]
Looking at the bigger picture, you’ll be leading the armies of the USSR, USA, and Germany, from the Wehrmacht’s Invasion of Poland to the Battle for Berlin. New battles will have more events and strategic decisions to make than those available before. For example, deciding to lay mines along one flank instead of the other will have an effect on the further course of the battle. Or maybe you’ll be able to hold an important strategic objective, or a bloody line of defence, which will give you access to a unique type of support that you may not have received otherwise. You’ll have to determine for yourself where and when to take risks, and whether they’re worth an extra push. Which flank will you throw your forces at? What are you keeping in reserve? It’ll all be up to you!

[h1]Further Intel on How Single-Player Missions Are Created[/h1]
Unfortunately, our format (and we already have a lot of text ːsteamhappyː) doesn’t allow us to go into more detail about the process of creating the maps, but we’ll gladly answer all of your questions on the single-player campaign in the comments on this piece of news on our social networks and in our forums. 

Until the next time!

===

[*]Upgrading available missions,
[*]Developing the campaign system (UI elements, briefings, global map, historical chronicles),
[*]Developing new missions.
[/list]
So, first of all, let’s take a look at:

[h1]Quality Standards[/h1]
As you’ve probably already noticed, we’ve hidden nearly all of the previously available missions in order to do further work on them. Our strategy in doing so is based on the results of internal studio play tests, analysis of player comments, and our periodic surveys.

The main issue we’re focusing on is ensuring proper UI quality. All events, the minimap and UI signals, pop-up messages and voice instructions will be synchronized, to help the player control the situation rather than make them feel panicked. 

We’re also doing lots of bug fixes here. For example, in Operation Niwi, it can happen that saboteurs manage to lay mines on the bunker only every other time. Sometimes, they just gather around it for a friendly chat while waiting for your next orders. Soldiers must strictly obey their commander’s orders, you know!

We might make a few changes to the player’s objectives as well.

[h1]Historical Immersion[/h1]
Those of you who’ve had a chance to play the previous Blitzkriegs might remember the briefings and the strategic maps, which really helped immerse you in the historical background of the games. In keeping with this fine tradition, we’re preparing something similarly interesting here, too. You’ll be able to embrace the whole theatre of operations with your eyes, watch fragments of real films made at the time, and read interesting descriptions of concomitant events. 

We’ll be able to properly evaluate the results of the campaign system’s implementation in the update after the next update. The plan is to give you access to this content in Version 0.7.0, along with a new map, Sevastopol.

[h1]The Battles to Come [/h1]
Looking at the bigger picture, you’ll be leading the armies of the USSR, USA, and Germany, from the Wehrmacht’s Invasion of Poland to the Battle for Berlin. New battles will have more events and strategic decisions to make than those available before. For example, deciding to lay mines along one flank instead of the other will have an effect on the further course of the battle. Or maybe you’ll be able to hold an important strategic objective, or a bloody line of defence, which will give you access to a unique type of support that you may not have received otherwise. You’ll have to determine for yourself where and when to take risks, and whether they’re worth an extra push. Which flank will you throw your forces at? What are you keeping in reserve? It’ll all be up to you!

[h1]Further Intel on How Single-Player Missions Are Created[/h1]
Unfortunately, our format (and we already have a lot of text ːsteamhappyː) doesn’t allow us to go into more detail about the process of creating the maps, but we’ll gladly answer all of your questions on the single-player campaign in the comments on this piece of news on our social networks and in our forums. 

Until the next time!

===

notes.title: Update 0.6.8
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2015/068MINIWEB.jpg[/IMG]

Attention! We have received new instructions from Development HQ on the method of entering battle, as well as an update on Generals. You can now also request redeployment to a different sector of the front. Take a look at the complete list of changes and more detailed information in the following message:
[list]
[*]Attacks against human players, assaults on AI bases and defence tests are now all on separate buttons. Player rankings remain the same.
[*]In accordance with player requests, any General can now take command of any type of unit, but can only effectively use and buff guard units matching his speciality. This change also affects support types, with some either becoming cheaper or partially modified. All Generals now have their own prize battles. These are consumed first, irrespective of the total pool of prize battles.
[*]Two new Generals per faction are now available. The Commander of Offensive Operations will allow you to perform fast-paced local blitzkriegs, while the Commander of Preparatory Fire will use artillery support with maximum efficiency, turning any battlefield into a scorched earth. Remember, we always want to hear your ideas for new generals, so be sure to drop a comment on this news wherever you see it!
[*]You can also now request redeployment for 10,000 Glory points. Command will determine a new sector of the front for you to prove yourself in.
[*]Attacking forces within deployment zones are now hidden behind a smoke screen, which prevents the defenders from hitting them. But be warned – attackers can shoot out through the smoke at surrounding defenders within range. The smoke will dispel when the attacking troops cross the area border, or after 2 minutes have passed. This should solve the problem of defenders camping around the deployment zone.
[*]All of the attacker’s units will now appear in ‘Hold position’ mode by default, and will remain like this while being entrenched when defences are placed. 
[*]Chat has been improved, with signals added when messages are received via Whisper or Reply.
[*]Added an option to place all types of units, fortifications, and obstructions on bridges.
[*]When an attack command is given by right clicking, it is not cancelled after the unit executes its movement commands.
[*]The camera scroll speed can now be adjusted in the settings. It will vary by default for all types of camera movements: WASD and arrows; push-scrolling, and moving with the middle mouse button.
[*]The pathfinding system has been improved in narrow places, which should improve the situation with lagging at high tiers.

notes.title: DevBlog 7
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/7miniweb.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Improving Combat Doctrine (Artyom, Lead Designer)[/h1]

I wanted to let you all know that we’re persistently polishing and improving the game based on player feedback.

Firstly, we’re implementing the map rotation mechanism, which will allow players to request transfers to different sectors of the front. This will cost 10,000 Glory (for now; this is still subject to change). By the way, current maps will be receiving a different number of supply points, in light of the current balance.

Secondly, extra measures will be taken to prevent the deployment of assault troops from being blocked. We already have a few ideas about this and are testing them even as I write this.

Thirdly, we’re working on the map boundaries. The black area will be reworked, and the map edges will become logically justified and reachable, for both defenders and attackers. By the way, here’s a work-in-progress version of some of these map changes:

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/7map.jpg[/IMG]

Fourthly, we’re updating mine mechanics. They’ll be more difficult to find, and some generals will be given great bonuses for their use.

Fifthly, we’re discussing the fortification upgrade mechanism. For example – pillboxes. Their role is to hinder the enemy with their durability, allowing more powerful units and fortifications to safely deal damage to attackers. In theory, we could add an option to choose what to emphasise in pillbox construction – wall thickness, or better weapons. We also have an idea about introducing separate supply points for fortifications. This would allow players to deploy their defences in a more strategic way.

To top it all off, we’re also working on small economy updates, like an option to rearm units for half their purchase cost.

It’s a lot of work, and we’re right in the thick of it!

===

notes.title: DevBlog 6
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/UMRLS.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]MLRS Field Testing (Artyom, Lead Game Designer)[/h1]

The vast majority of players welcomed our in-game implementation of rocket artillery, but, due to their comments on our information networks, we’ve concluded that these units need some improvements. And so, without any delay, we’re asking you to take part in an extra survey that you will find in the game.

[h1]Correcting Turns in Pathfinding (Nikolay, Lead Programmer)[/h1]

Pathfinding is one of the most complex and intricate systems in this project. Over the last couple of years, we only introduced some minor changes that couldn’t drastically improve the situation as a whole. However, we’re now optimizing the pathfinding system at a whole new level. In addition to extra time and effort, we’ve hired a dedicated specialist to work exclusively on this task. Last month he managed to considerably optimize some algorithms, namely those related to vehicles making turns. You can evaluate these changes in the latest update.

Our future plans are even more grandiose, but it would be difficult to explain them without using mathematical analysis terminology, so we’ll just hit the main points.

Programmers have a special name for particularly tangled code: “spaghetti code.” Right now we are working on untangling this digital spaghetti in the pathfinding system.

We will also clear our code of little bugs and improve the group pathfinding system (algorithms for joint unit movement, unit combat participation, and searching for alternative paths).

As a result, vehicles will become smarter, and it will now be a joy to control them. In order to show you how difficult the whole process is and what the cost of the tiniest error is, I’ve picked a GIF animation that I would like to show you: :)
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/pathfinding.gif[/IMG]

[h1]Continuing to Fix Bugs (Jean, Lead Tester)[/h1]

The closer our release date is, the more attention we have to pay to fixing bugs and improving the project’s technical reliability. Today I would like to tell you about an error that we have named “High Jump.” It cropped up at the mortar detachment in the Operation Niwi mission. It would be best for you to see it with your own eyes...
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/gifbug.gif[/IMG]

===

notes.title: Update 0.6.7
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog41.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Comrade, you have an MLRS at your command![/h1]

Commander, we are happy to inform you that Multiple Launch Rocket Systems are now at your disposal. You can even give them a try right now on the new Tier 7 PvP King of the Hill map! Besides this, Command HQ needs you to carry out PvE Operation Spreewald – rescue prisoners of war and retrieve top secret documents while you’re at it. To help you achieve these goals, you will have Generals of Artillery and of Sabotage Operations at your disposal. 

Among other things, our experts have been working on training the vehicle crews. They now respond to orders better, and no longer lose speed when moving along complex trajectories. With their new instructions, they’ll no longer be homing in on enemy hedgehogs, barbed wire, statues, and other non-aggressive objects. We have also worked on improving communications between unit commanders: a message history tab has been added to chat (players can now see the last 100 chat messages), as well as a Combat Chat tab in which players can send messages to each other in Active Defence mode.

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/0/618459931321255936/#c523897653303355289]Actual list of bugs on 0.6.7 update[/url]

You can view the complete list of changes in the full dispatch from our Communication Centre:
[LIST]
[*]Now, when a unit is rearmed to a new tier, all of its upgrades remain. Experience obtained by units will still be recalculated.
[*]Unit sorting has been improved in the central panel, both on base and in combat. Units are now arranged as follows: Type -> Tier -> Upgrade Gears -> Unit Level
[*]Shadow borders have been reworked on all maps.
[*]Added USSR Mission #6, Spreewald, to the mission selection interface. In this mission, we liberate camp prisoners and capture documents that are important to High Command.
[*]Added a new Tier 7 map: King of the Hill. All new players who reach a level 7 base will be transferred to this map. When the maps are rebalanced, the chances of moving to this map will be reduced.
[*]A new unit class, Rocket Artillery, is now available on Tier 7: the BM-13 Katyusha for the USSR, the Sherman Calliope for the Allies, and the Panzerwerfer 42 Auf.Sf for Germany. An MLRS can use a rocket salvo to fire at a target from a long distance.
[*]Two new generals are available for each faction: the Artillery General and the Special Ops General, each with his own features.
[*]To improve our pathfinding system, we have optimized the movement of vehicles when turning. Now units respond to orders better and no longer lose speed when moving along a complex trajectory.
[*]Now vehicles ignore enemy hedgehogs, barbed wire, statues, and other non-aggressive objects as targets and do not home onto them.
[*]A message history has been added to chat so that players can now see the last 100 chat messages.
[*]Chat has been added to combat. The Combat Chat tab in synchronized sessions allows players to send messages to each other.
[/LIST]


===

notes.title: Report on the most recent player vote #1
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/engres.jpg[/IMG]

Dear soldiers,
Here’s our report on the most recent player vote (last week’s survey in the game’s main menu). We had several items in the survey:
[list]
[*]How is the single player campaign’s difficulty level after the recent changes to the combat system?
[*]Who is stronger in Active Defence mode?
[*]Should we make support actions unit abilities?
[/list]

In the end, the following decisions were made:
[list]
[*]40% of players think the single player campaign is too difficult, so we’re going to make it easier to earn the first star on its missions.
[*]33% of players believe that the attacker is stronger in Active Defence, 37% chose the defender, and 30% think that they are equally matched. Game balance is definitely going in the right direction. We will soon study our faction balance and conduct additional surveys.
[*]81% are insistent on implementing support actions as unit abilities, which we will definitely do!
[/list]

Thanks to everyone who took part in this event! Please participate in the game’s development by casting your vote!


===

notes.title: DevBlog 5: Error Correction
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/gif1.gif[/IMG]

We have reached the point where the amount of error correction and polishing of existing features outweighs the introduction of new game mechanics. So Episode 5 of Developer Diaries will deal with the testing department’s work and the highest priority key issues to be addressed in upcoming versions. Our future episodes will focus on the game’s appearance by its release date.
 
[h1]How It Works[/h1]
Many people believe that a tester’s work is an endless boring series of checking the same game components over and over again—and they are probably right. Except that it’s not so boring. What’s more, occasionally testers not only make changes in the game to fix bugs but introduce some functional mini-features. For example, if you have played for a hundred hours and faced one and the same annoying control issue, you can suggest an effective way to solve it. We can recall one such case during the development of Blitzkrieg: previously, double right-clicking selected all units of a certain type on the map. Now they are only selected in the screen area, which allows you to control your forces on two fronts, even with “temporary” squads not assigned to hotkeys. 
 
[h1]Especially Evil Errors[/h1]
The true art of catching errors manifests itself in especially sophisticated situations. For example, we encountered an error that could take down the whole cluster. The cause was not obvious, although players regularly managed to disturb us in our sleep with the issue. It turned out in the end that the error was caused by a specific type of unit collision. If two infantry squads were in a narrow passage that was not wider than a tank and a tank tried to go through them, the infantrymen clipped into each other and brought down the server.

[h1]What We Are Working On Right Now[/h1]
We are constantly fixing many errors and improving existing functions, so we would like to tell you what we are working on right now. It may not be true that we will fix these in the next version (besides, our list of issues is constantly changing), but right now the following set of tasks is at the highest priority:
[list]
[*]A command to attack a target should not be cancelled by a command to move
[*]Improving the matchmaking situation for everyone
[*]Solving the issue when an enemy is attacked in a narrow passage by several vehicle units
[*]Allowing howitzers and mortars to fire at a point and not just a target
[*]Fixing attack target priorities for all units
[*]Fixing uncontrolled infantry crawling 
[*]Making the Generals interface more informative and comfortable (from the levelling-up process displayed in the General’s file to XP received based on battle results)
[*]Player rankings should be displayed in battle
[*]The type of battle (synchronous or asynchronous) should be clearly shown to players 
[*]Fixing the display of the game version in the main menu
[/list]

[h1]Bugs come in different kinds, and they are fixed by different people (Vitaly, Lead Artist)[/h1]
Our bugs are boring when compared to those that our testing department encounters. As a rule, we usually have to redraw something. Right now we are getting a lot of routine work like this. I’d like to show you something in particular, but I’m afraid it wouldn't be very interesting. For example, we finished working on Wojtek. Unlike the comic Fool’s Day version, he is now more realistic. Without his anthropomorphic features, he has become an ordinary bear. We are also getting the self-propelled Karl-Gerät mortar ready, but we’ll have to show that a bit later. So, this week the funny GIF image is mine. :)
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/gif2.gif[/IMG]

[h1]An Interface Worthy of Generals (Sergey, Interface Designer)[/h1]
The current implementation of the Generals interfaces could very well be called temporary. The mechanics of obtaining Generals, together with all of the tooltips and skill descriptions, will be greatly improved in next to no time, improved until they’re “dressed to kill.” We will also introduce a user-friendly system for levelling up a General’s skills. :) 
The “green frame” currently shows what skill will be upgraded when reaching the next General’s level. We are not planning to remove it. Unavailable skills will become black and white, and explanatory tooltips will contain info like the name of a skill, its strength, upgrade requirements, and its description.

[h1]Maps are not without bugs, either (Andrey, Lead Map Designer)[/h1]
We have worked an awful lot on our battlefields, but there is still a good amount to be done. In addition to our upcoming wayfinding improvement, we have widened passages to make units behave more satisfactory. By the way, some completely unexpected factors have sometimes resulted in extremely strange behaviour on the maps. For example, a sense of beauty previously made one of the map designers (especially when we were working on the Swamp map, everyone’s “favourite”) use a lot of small items, even those sometimes barely visible. So, for example, a small stone in the centre of the road could turn into an insurmountable obstacle when in the path of a battle vehicle, causing the whole crew to fall in a fit.

notes.title: DevBlog 4: Generals
notes.content:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/USA1.jpg[/IMG]

The main idea behind the Generals is to create diverse gameplay by different sets of units and abilities that result in special combat tactics and variable combat situations. Previously, players were able to create ‘all-purpose armies’ that didn’t have any particular strengths or weaknesses, and this often led to homogeneous sets of units fighting with identical tactics. So by giving players an opportunity to define the strengths or weaknesses of their armies, we’re changing the eventual pattern of combat completely.

[h1]How We Did It[/h1]
All units and support types play their own part in combat. We began by categorising them, so that we could provide the Generals with specific tools for the battlefield. For example, the Scout support, armoured cars and snipers were all assigned to the Scouting category (they’re just examples by the way, that’s not the full list!). So every General receives one item from each category, thus becoming stronger and more effective in some respects, and weaker in others. To intensify this effect, we created unique upgrades for units under a General’s command. For example, the speed of medium tanks was increased for the General of Tanks.

[h1]Real People[/h1]
Originally, the Generals were not going to have any recognisable historical prototypes. But to create a more authentic atmosphere and expand on the game’s educational aspects, we decided finally to introduce the Generals as real historical figures, with their own personal histories viewable in their personnel files.

[h1]Implementing Community Feedback[/h1]
By the time we’d introduced the Generals feature in the game, players had already developed their own preferences and tended to field their own favourite unit formations. But the Generals took some of the existing tools away from the players, and that caused them a certain amount of discomfort. So we’ve been carefully considering the players’ feedback on the matter, and the next game version will see a new iteration of this feature, improved to meet some of the community’s desires. For example, the most popular wish is to be able to play for any General, with all types of units, to mitigate the restrictions imposed by this specific balancing act. So we’ll be implementing this possibility through the Generals’ talents system. Regardless of which General you choose, all types of units and support will be available to you. However, the unique upgrades your General’s specialized units and support receive will be more effective, while non-specialized units and support will be re-balanced through increased cost and reduced effectiveness.

[h1]Further Development on Generals[/h1]
The Generals will be receiving new features and class possibilities in the future. In particular, we’re now thinking about introducing a new type of skills for Generals that will provide our decorated military leaders with greater and more powerful tools. These can be absolutely different skills and abilities – from unique actions to improved attack times. For example, unique tank camouflage, for hiding in forests. And speaking of new classes, the next update will allow you to invite the General of Artillery into your headquarters, to provide you with the most effective artillery support.

[h1]Andrey, Lead Level Designer[/h1]
When we were working on the new single-player missions, we encountered a funny bug that visualized the law of conservation of energy: all the soil dug out to make the trenches became heaped into one large pile on the map!
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog345.jpg[/IMG]
By the way, players will soon be able to test the multiplayer ‘King of the Hill’ map :)

[h1]Vitaly, Lead Artist[/h1]
We taught the infantry how to jump into trenches in a really beautiful way, worked on the appearance of the Generals, and ‘enlivened’ the missile artillery.
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog42.jpg[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog43.jpg[/IMG]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog41.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Nikolay, Lead Programmer[/h1]
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/Nikolay.gif[/IMG]
===

notes.title: DevBlog 3: After Implementing the Update
notes.content:
[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8580&d=1440786112[/IMG]

[B]New Tooltips[/B]

If you have already had a chance to try Update 0.6.6, you might have noticed that unit tooltips have changed.

This UI component previously showed little information and raised more questions than it gave answers. Our task was to fit a large amount of information into a small window before the new combat system was introduced. We understood how important it was not only to bring you information that would be useful for gameplay (such as “this unit is effective against that unit”) but also to introduce some of the historical education that everyone is expecting from us.
As a result, all information shown in a tooltip has been divided into the following sections:
[LIST]
[*]Unit description (what units are used for, i.e. the key to using them effectively)
[*]Durability (or hit points)
[*]Armour (for vehicles only: front, side, and back armour thickness in mm)
[*]Weapons (two types, as a rule: primary and secondary)
[/LIST]

Players can research unit improvements (Gears) in the Engineering Works. Upgrades are different for vehicles and infantry. For instance, we enhance optics for tanks, but we increase shooting accuracy for infantry. Now, instead of displaying the total effect of all upgrades, we show a simplified version of that information, where strokes represent the number of identical upgrades for each type of unit. This also makes the information easier to process.

Not everything with the new tooltips has been polished yet, and they might contain errors. We’ll be glad if you point them out for us. In the meantime, we are planning a lot of chat improvements that will be implemented step by step. These include: fixing bugs; correcting the colour of messages, nicknames, and tiers; preserving status, position, and active tab in chat when the player leaves it; introducing various minor transparency fixes, highlighting a tab when it receives a new message, and changing the position of chat headlines.

We also are preparing the combat selection UI (battle vs. AI, battle vs. real players, defence test) and thinking about texturing the UI (we’d like to add damage, roughness, and so on. We will probably be making these amendments very soon, but they will hardly be major changes, just cosmetic ones).
...
[B]to be continued soon :)[/B]

notes.title: Update 0.6.6.
notes.content:
Commanders!

In order to enhance combat efficiency of the Allied Armed Forces, you can now appoint battle-tested generals to command your infantry, aircraft, and tank units. George S. Patton, Henry H. Arnold, Bernard Law Montgomery and other prominent officers will now lead your glorious army to victory over the German aggressors.

In addition, the High Command of Nival stated the completion of massive rebalancing measures. Now, operational characteristics of vehicles are reproduced with the highest historical accuracy.

Important note: our French and German users may have problems with localization. To be able to read descriptions of Generals, please select English language in the Main Menu. We will fix this bug within a short period of time

[B]Added Cologne, a new historical mission for the Allies. [/B]
The player must clear the city of the German forces still remaining after extended bombardment. The battle is set against the background of the beautiful Cologne Cathedral under continuous missile artillery fire. We have also added English and German voiceovers to some missions.

[B]Generals added. [/B]
All players have now access to a default General, a General of Tanks, a General of Infantry, and a General of Aircraft. Each military leader has excellent skills that improve the stats of both individual units and all detachments under his command. For example, the US Air Force under "Hap" Arnold's command cooperates well with ground forces and can prove its worth in offensive combat, while Montgomery can form ground vehicles and defensive fortifications into a steel first, making your base an impregnable fortress. We should note that the Strategic and Deluxe Editions include exclusive Generals. When in combat, Generals gain experience, which is required for them to level up. Levelling up a General improves the stats that he provides to his units and unlocks new types of tactical support.

[B]The balance of all units has been completely revised to reflect historical reality. [/B]
All units' stats and performance characteristics are now closer to their historical values. This revision applies not only to vehicles but to infantry units as well. For example, Soviet infantry have received an extra unit, while US infantry has had one unit removed.

[B]Players now have access to two extra bases belonging to other factions, which they can upgrade in parallel with their main one. [/B]
If you want to go to a different base, select the corresponding item in the Esc menu. When one of the bases is selected, all others become "frozen," i.e. they cannot be attacked or get any resources.

[B]Matchmaking changes.[/B]
Over the last month, all players were earning their rating. Now this will be the main factor that influences matchmaking. The matchmaking system will also take into account the player's base development level.

[B]Added trenches.[/B]
We have added to the game the option to dig trenches and place an infantry squad inside. When in a trench, infantry take less damage. You can take infantry out of a trench at any moment and send them into combat. Enemy trenches can be taken if you kill the enemies inside them.

[B]Chat changes.[/B]
The chat design has been changed to be less intrusive and more ergonomic.

[B]New living creatures.[/B]
There are new living beings on some maps, including animals enjoying every minute of their existence.

[B]Sniper girls.[/B]
Now all Soviet sniper squads include two beautiful girls ready to destroy enemy personnel at the drop of a hat.

[B]Soldiers with AT rifles.[/B]
Soviet anti-tank infantry now have AT rifles on the first three tiers to fight against armoured vehicles with. On subsequent tiers, they are armed with lend-lease rocket launchers.

[B]UI changes.[/B]
When hovering over or upgrading a unit, real performance characteristics are displayed, along with any changes to in-game stats that are directly related to them.

[B]Fortification management.[/B]
We have added an option to manage your fortifications in Active Defence mode and select targets for them to attack.

[B]Moving backwards.[/B]
The odd game logic where a vehicle seemed to choose on its own which side would face in the proper direction when moving to a specified point has been replaced by manual controls. Now you have a corresponding key (B by default) on the command panel to move backwards. You can also move a tank backwards by holding the CTRL key and right-clicking on the target location. When you send a vehicle the normal way, it will always move forward.

notes.title: DevBlog 2: Our New Combat System
notes.content:
[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8479&d=1440099680[/IMG]

[B]We’ve completely reworked our combat system in the most recent version, especially the interaction between different models of vehicles. How did we do this, and what are the gameplay implications?[/B]

[B]Armour Protection and Ricochets[/B]
The old combat system had a lot of drawbacks, both from the player’s perspective and from that of our own internal development. However, this helped us to establish a basic balance line, and starting from that we can now configure units as we wish and give them stats that resemble real ones as closely as possible while maintaining the balance between the models. This has allowed us to start moving towards greater historical accuracy in vehicle firefights. We currently have:
[LIST]
[*]Realistic armour from all sides. Previously there were situations where shells ricocheted off of heavy tanks even if they hit the rear or the side, where the armour was definitely not thick enough to protect the tank from a sufficiently large-calibre shell.*
[*]Realistic breakthrough setting. In most cases, APC machine guns no longer penetrate tanks. Tanks do, however, still have vulnerable points (poor rear armour, armour joints, gaps under turrets), and an APC can deal damage to the tank crew or disable the tank’s modules in certain situations.*
[*]It is now simply impossible to damage some vehicle models with a frontal attack. Monsters of engineering like the T95 and IS-3 are invulnerable if used competently.
[*]In addition, the number of ricochets in tank battles is now closer to real life. Low-tier small-calibre cannons don’t have a chance of penetrating vehicles with better armour protection.*
[*]Ricochets no longer do damage.*
[/LIST]

[B]How We Created Historical Armour[/B]
The RTS genre has both technical and gameplay limitations. We couldn’t make a 3D model of a tank consisting of plates of different thickness and shoot at a random plate at a random angle. That makes no sense in our game. So we used statistical simulation, taking into account the following factors:
[LIST]
[*]The thickness of every tank armour plate
[*]The structural angles of inclination (and therefore effective thickness of the tank armour)
[*]The composition of the armour plates. I.e. if one side of a tank is covered with one thick plate and one thin plate, then the chance of breaking through directly depends on the chances of hitting one plate or the other.
[*]The accuracy of weapons and guidance systems. This is manifested in two different ways in the new combat system: a gun can simply aim at the tank or can target a specific weak area of the tank.
[/LIST]
Like most mathematical models, ours is obviously based on certain assumptions that can be slightly inaccurate. For instance, the tanks’ relative combat distances. Hit and breakthrough statistics heavily depend on whether the combat distance was 500, 1000 or 2000 meters. Parameters like this can make our model less accurate, but we plan to keep going and will continue to adjust the combat system until it is acceptable and we have the necessary adjustment tools.

[B]Vehicle Speed/Mobility and Misses[/B]
As we moved tank stats closer to historical ones, we didn’t forget about their movement speed and turret rotation speed. Differences in the power of engines and turret drives are also reflected in the game. But that’s not all. As we developed the idea of statistical simulation, we decided to take into account the mobility and size of tanks, too. It’s more difficult to hit a moving target, and the quicker it moves, the more difficult it is. That’s how it works in real life. We decided not to apply any dodge buffs to moving tanks, since it wouldn’t be right to make players control their vehicles non-stop and move them continuously to avoid missing out on such a buff. Blitzkrieg is a game of strategy and planning, not micromanagement. But we still considered the size and possible speed of vehicles when we adjusted our hit calculation methods, thus accentuating the combat peculiarities of specific tanks.

[B]Gameplay Changes[/B]
We want to kill two birds with one stone with our new combat system. First, this will make your game experience better. We all like historical accuracy, even when it doesn’t have any significant influence on gameplay. Second, the historical characteristics themselves highlight key tactics. Now that heavy tanks and tank destroyers are really impenetrable from the front, positional warfare and manoeuvres become more important. The role of medium tanks automatically shifts to infantry support tanks or breakthrough tanks, just like it was in real battles. In addition, the individually configured vehicles allow us to maintain the significance of earlier models. It might make sense to keep a couple of lighter and faster tanks instead of replacing them with later models, so that you can shoot tank destroyers from behind if you manage to break through to the enemy’s rear.
As a whole, the mechanics of the interaction between different unit classes has been completely changed. Counter-units are now stronger against their targets. This automatically increases the value of counter-counter-units. And all of this completely changes the tactics to follow when adding units to squads and keeping one or another unit type in battle. Along with Generals, this will completely change combat tactics in Blitzkrieg 3. Players who properly plan their tactics before battle and skilfully manage their units in battle will be rewarded.

[B]Artyom, Lead Game Designer[/B]
I’d only like to add that we’ve arduously tested the new balance system since introducing historical performance characteristics, and Generals. It should be noted that we like the balance of the sides as they are now, but the balance of the Generals makes us feel like this:
[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8478&d=1440086445[/IMG]

[B]Andrey, Lead Level Designer[/B]
We made a large number of modifications to the map. You know, I think that instead of talking about it, it’ll be better if I just show you the symbiosis of the artists’ work and the level designers’ work – this is from when we were adjusting the lighting on the Cologne map (bottom photo - before adjusting the lighting; the top photo is after adjusting the lighting).

[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8473&d=1440085748[/IMG]

[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8474&d=1440085748[/IMG]

[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8475&d=1440085761[/IMG]

[B]Vitaly, Lead Artist; Nikolay, Lead Programmer; Jean, Lead Tester[/B]
[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8477&d=1440086286[/IMG]
We’re getting ready to deliver the current version :)

====

notes.title: Update 0.6.5
notes.content:
[h1][b]Good Day Comrades![/b][/h1]

[H1]What’s New.[/H1]

•	Tier 7 (this HQ upgrade costs 148500) unlocks three new maps: Dam, Large Coal Quarry, and Hills. Each map has three control points and one base.

•	As we prepare to implement faction differences, we have rebalanced the units, allowing us to make interactions between classes more realistic. You can view the complete list of changes at the [url=http://en.blitzkrieg.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1954]following link[/url].

•	We have added Anzio, a fourth historical mission for the Allies that concentrates on urban combat. 

•	We have added the Construction Crew, a new type of support costing one charge, and allowing you to disarm mines or dismantle Czech hedgehogs.

•	The tutorial is now made up of several steps, and players can choose sections most relevant to them and skip the others.

•	Ratings are now calculated correctly, and a single combined rating is used for defence and attack.

•	If you own the Strategic or Deluxe Edition, you’ll be able to build a monument to one of your faction’s great leaders: Lenin for the USSR, Lincoln for the Allies, and Bismarck for Germany. This costs 500 resources.

•	You can no longer challenge an opponent to battle in chat more than once per minute. The attacker will always receive a message if the opponent declines the battle.

•	The chat nicknames of players who bought the Deluxe Edition are now displayed in silver.

•	The chat nicknames of players who bought the Strategic Edition are now displayed in gold.

•	In the UI, the number of units deployed by the attacker and the defender is now shown instead of displaying the enemy’s stored resources.

•	Now, when searching for opponents using the Assault button, players can’t attack bases in their own factions; however, attacking your own faction is available through chat.

•	If a player hasn’t completed a single mission, they will be invited to play PvE at the base once per day. If they haven’t played PvP, they will be invited just as often to join multiplayer from the mission selection screen.

•	We have improved our pathfinding system, allowing us to fix the issue where infantry got stuck on bridges and in cliffs.

•	If a player is at the base and the game is minimized, they will receive a sound message notifying them that they’re being attacked, and the game icon will flash in the taskbar.

•	If an attempt to attack is made and the opponent has no units deployed for defence, they will be informed of this after agreeing to the session. The player can then either observe the attack (with an empty troop pool) or decline and let the attacker carry out an asynchronous attack.

•	A new tab for future generals has been added to the central panel.

•	The info screen is displayed in the main menu once per day, the first time you log in. 

•	Now you can move faster around the map by holding the middle mouse button in a session or the left mouse button at the base. Movement speed has been doubled.

notes.title: Real-time PvP is on
notes.content:
For the first time in the history of the genre, Blitzkrieg 3 features a multiplayer game mode based on the “attack vs. defense” principle. This asymmetry, typical of World War II combat operations, is the basis for Blitzkrieg 3’s multiplayer. 

Developing an Active Base Defense mode where one side attacks the defender’s fortified positions was a complex and interesting task, one contributed to by Blitzkrieg 3’s game community, whose assistance can scarcely be overstated. Players’ requests seriously influenced our development plans. Today we are responding to them with a new multiplayer mode where both the attacking and defending forces are under the control of real-life opponents. 

[h1] You can view the full list of the changes we’ve implemented below. [/h1]

[b]● A new multiplayer mode, Active Base Defense, has been added. [/b]
Leading your troops to assault enemy fortifications has become even more interesting since defensive forces can be commanded by a real life opponent! If a player’s base is under attack, they get a notification suggesting they lead the defense of their position in person or delegate this entertaining task to the AI instead. 

[b]● The matchmaking system is set to search for the online opponent with the highest priority. [/b]
This will allow us to test the new game mode more carefully. 

[b]● Global chat has been added to the game, with the option to attack an opponent by clicking on their nickname. [/b]
Thanks to our communication troops’ skill and selfless work, commanders of military units now have access to a single common frequency band to communicate and coordinate their actions. It should be kept in mind, however, that enemy forces can intercept these radio messages, resulting in their attacking the commander’s base. 

[b]● Training your regular army in engineering. [/b]
Regular infantry units have at their disposal engineering specialists, whose main task is to train recruits. Now regular infantry squads are able to disarm minefields and deal effectively with anti-tank hedgehogs. 

[b]● Say No to marauders and plunderers! [/b]
The Supreme High Command has resolved to stop unrestrained plundering in occupied territories. Now players get resources from Command as a reward for successfully completing combat operations. Rewards are determined by General HQ and don’t depend on the amount of resources that the enemy has. 

[b]● General HQ’s orders to attack an enemy are final and not subject to any appeal. [/b]
Once players press the Assault button and choose their opponent, they cannot switch to any other opponent. In wartime conditions, the Supreme High Command’s orders are observed without question. 

[b]● Withdrawal of all industrial and utility facilities over the front line.[/b]
Command thinks it dangerous to store considerable amounts of vital resources and produce military equipment in the immediate vicinity of the front line. The Commander in Chief has ordered the withdrawal of Tank Factories and Fuel/Material Depots to the rear. Military equipment and infantry units are put at players’ disposal as reinforcements requiring a certain amount of fuel to transport them from the rear to the front line.

notes.title: Real-time PvP is coming!
notes.content:
From the Blitzkrieg 3 Design Office: defense and attack against real enemies.

Comrades, we are happy to announce a long-awaited update that fully satisfies the requests of our front-line commanders. First of all, we have added the option to fight against a real enemy both in game chat and on the battlefield. After receiving a notification that your base has been attacked, you begin fighting the enemy’s advancing troops.

We have made an important decision: moving depots and factories from the front line to the rear. Only buildings required for the use of human and technical resources ordered from General HQ remain on the base.
Regular infantry units have been retrained and can now successfully deal with minefields, hedgehogs.  

Time is a commander’s biggest enemy, which the new timer will remind you of in the final minutes, as enemy artillery and air forces wipe the attacking army off the face of the earth in a single sweep.

Global chat has been added to maintain a high level of coordination of commanders’ actions on the front lines. You can attack an opponent in game chat by clicking on their nickname. For the sake of convenience, factions and players are divided into different colours.

notes.title: Blitzkrieg Summer Sale
notes.content:
My fellow American and European friends!

Today, while the power and resources of all our nations are concentrated on new battlefronts in Blitzkrieg 3, our Western allies begin their Steam Summer Sale to support our rear guard defences. The Nival High Command is keen to join this outstanding initiative by our American comrades. So by order of the General Quartermaster, we therefore present some excellent discounts across the entire Blitzkrieg series!

From today and up to 22nd June, Blitzkrieg 3 will be discounted by 10%, with the original Blitzkrieg and Blitzkrieg 2 discounted by 75%. The might of our battlefield weapons and the strategic genius of our generals have been shown on many occasions in the past. Today, we are taking this to new levels with Blitzkrieg 3, the greatest game in the series to date, which is currently pitting general against general in Early Access.

Our thanks to the great support of our game communities in the United States, Europe and Russia who are helping us to achieve our goal of Blitzkrieg 3 becoming the new benchmark for Real Time Strategy games, bringing acclaim and innovation to the genre.

This war is ours! See you on the battlefields of Blitzkrieg!

notes.title: Update 0.6.4 / Обновление 0.6.4
notes.content:
Good Day Comrades!
After our last update development team has been making great progress.
In cooperation with the Main Command of the Armed Forces we have developed two new PVE scenarios and successfully re-balanced the existing one. We have implemented a radical revision of the existing game balancing along with the economics system and resolved a large number of other issues.

[h1]Here is the full list of changes and improvements[/h1]

[B]What’s new?[/B]
[list]
[*]New historical mission “Operation Niwi”.
[*]New historical mission “Kustrin Fortress”.
[*]Historical mission “Neisse Crossing” has been re-balanced.
[*]Control points acquisition rewards have been redistributed. Each next captured control point provides more resources than the previous one.
[*]New information panel added to the in base-view when no building is selected.
[*]New support type – “Incendiary projectile”.
[*]New support type – “Tank reinforcement”.
[*]New support type – “Infantry reinforcement”.
[*]New faction 3D-scene in main menu added.
[*]New icons for buildings and fortifications.
[/list]

[B]Balance and Economics changes[/B]
[list]
[*]Recourses per hour acquisition rate has been increased.
[*]Buildings prerequisites have been simplified.
[*]From Tier 4 onwards, the amount of support points has been increased. 
[*]Units power growth rate connected with new Tier acquisition has been increased from 1.38 to 1.5.
[*]Some units’ cost has increased.
[*]SU-85 reloading time has decreased from 4.5 to 3.45. The damage has decreased accordingly.
[*]The damage radius of tank machine-guns has decreased from 35 to 30.
[*]The session time across all Tiers has increased by one minute.
[/list]

[B]Resolved issues[/B]
[list]
[*]Fortified tank near the building did not attack the infantry placed on its sides.
[*]The experience amount gained by dealing damage was too low.
[*]GUI did not display resources expenses per battle.
[*]Damage dealt to “Landing troops” was too low.
[*]“End battle” button needed to be clicked twice.
[*]Hill-based fortifications were displayed not as expected.
[*]Anti-tank infantry damage radius was displayed incorrectly.
[*]Dead infantry animations sometimes were displayed incorrectly.   
[*]x3 resources bonus was displayed after non-prize battles.
[*]Bunkers did not attack infantry in buildings.
[/list]

[B]Known issues[/B]
[list]
[*]Bonuses acquired by upgrading units in the Science center are in the re-balancing stage and have some issues with displaying.
[*]Bunched units do not attack the enemy without an order.
[*]Possible game crashes while constantly Alt-Tabbing.
[*]Terrain buff affects infantry in buildings.
[*]Units from the same squad can have different grenade-throw speeds.
[*]Verifying the integrity of game cache leads to downloading 97 game files.
[*]Launcher interface localization is in progress.
[*]Bunkers cannot be mined.
[*]Assault infantry throw anti-tank grenades with a large delay.
[*]Low frame rate with in-game explosion effects.
[*]Assault infantry fires armored vehicles.
[*]Camera map-marker mismatches with real camera position.
[/list]

[h1]Other languages[/h1]

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/4/598198173698161766/]Патчноуты на русском языке[/url]

notes.title: Update 0.6.3 / Обновление 0.6.3
Update 0.6.3 / Обновление 0.6.3
New Directives
notes.content:
[b]Dear friends![/b]
Since the “Blitzkrieg 3” SEA release we have received a lot of comments and suggestions from our players.
Alongside our community, we overcame a heavy workload that determined the direction of Blitzkrieg 3’s upcoming evolution.
 
Many new features are going to be added:

[b]Synchronous PvP mode.[/b]
We are glad to announce new multiplayer modes where players will now have the opportunity to battle armies led by human opponents in real-time:
1. Classical RTS 1v1 battles, where both players attempt to conquer each other with limited amount of units and resources. Total enemy annihilation is the main goal in this mode.
2. Attack enemy bases and defend your own in real-time.
If your base is under attack while you are in the game, you will have an opportunity to lead your defending troops yourself. If you are going to attack a hostile base, be prepared to fight not with an AI opponent, but with a human one.
New multiplayer modes are currently in active development and we will be pleased to tell you more about them in the near future.

[b]New Historical missions.[/b]
This June players will have an opportunity to challenge their strategic skills in new historical missions.
Three missions will be added, one for each side of the conflict. The Campaign interface will also be reworked.

[b]The Generals. [/b]  
We continue to work on the tactical aspect of the game, adding a variety of improvements. Generals are the new gameplay component with the aim to make every battle unique and unrepeatable. 
Generals features:
- Define the support and unit types players can use in their current battle
- Provide different bonuses to appropriate unit types. From accuracy improvements to unique special abilities
- Affect quality and quantity of player defenses
- Gain unique attack and defensive behavior patterns
- While gaining battle experience, Generals level grows and new abilities can be obtained.

[b]Opportunity to play for every side of the conflict. Faction units distinction.[/b]
Players will be able to develop up to three bases at any one time: Western Allies, Germany and USSR with separate progress for each.  With this feature faction units distinction will be added.

[b]Engineers.[/b]
Common infantry units will be reinforced with engineers who can bear mines and Czech hedgehogs. For players that do not play with common infantry, we will add another type of engineer as support.

[b]Historical changes.[/b] 
The damage of machine guns against tanks will be significantly decreased.
USSR early tier troops will be armed not with grenade launchers but with native anti-tank rifles.

[b]Localization improvements.[/b]
All in-game text and speech will be reworked and become more pleasant to the ears of native speakers.

And more!

[h1]Please post your feedback here:[/h1] 
http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/0/617336568064578432/

[h1]Обсуждение на русском языке здесь:[/h1] http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/1/617336568064571614/

[b]Opportunity to play for every side of the conflict. Faction units distinction.[/b]
Players will be able to develop up to three bases at any one time: Western Allies, Germany and USSR with separate progress for each.  With this feature faction units distinction will be added.

[b]Engineers.[/b]
Common infantry units will be reinforced with engineers who can bear mines and Czech hedgehogs. For players that do not play with common infantry, we will add another type of engineer as support.

[b]Historical changes.[/b] 
The damage of machine guns against tanks will be significantly decreased.
USSR early tier troops will be armed not with grenade launchers but with native anti-tank rifles.

[b]Localization improvements.[/b]
All in-game text and speech will be reworked and become more pleasant to the ears of native speakers.

And more!

notes.title: Update 0.6.2 / Обновление 0.6.2
Update 0.6.2 / Обновление 0.6.2
Blitzkrieg 3 - Update 0.6.1.
notes.content:
This update is designed to fix two major technical issues we have, as well as to bring some game changes and improvements. 

[b]Bugs fixed:[/b]
[list]
[*]The bug with "freezing" the game session at 100% combat loading is fixed. If this problem comes up again - within an hour after its appearance, it will be corrected automatically and will no longer prevent you from playing.
[*]The bug with combining accounts with "incorrect symbols" in the nicknames is fixed. Changing nickname procedure while binding the active Closed Alpha account to Steam is obligatory now.
[*]A number of minor technical bugs fixed.
[/list]

[b]Common:[/b]
Right now we are testing our anti-bot system, so there is a limitation of the amount of battles a day. Yet with this update it has been significantly increased: now you will be getting the resources for the victory in up to 100 attacks a day (instead of 25). 

[b]Support:[/b]
The cost of air support at the 5th level of development significantly decreased: 3 points for reconnaissance aircraft (instead of 5), and 4 points for assault aircrafts (instead of 6).
